हेमांभोजासनासीनं कृष्णं त्रैलोक्यमोहनम् ॥
1.80.m:
in an auspicious circle of jewels radiant with the splendor of the rising sun,
seated on a golden lotus seat, Kṛṣṇa, the enchanter of the three worlds,

1.80.s:
munivṛndaiḥ parivṛtamātmatattvavinirṇaye /
tebhyo munibhyaḥ svaṃ dhāma diśantaṃ paramakṣaram //
1.80.d:
मुनिवृन्दैः परिवृतमात्मतत्त्वविनिर्णये ।
तेभ्यो मुनिभ्यः स्वं धाम दिशन्तं परमक्षरम् ॥
1.80.m:
surrounded by hosts of sages to ascertain the truth of the Self,
pointing out his own supreme and imperishable abode to those sages;

1.80.s:
unnidredīvaraśyāmaṃ padmapatrāyatekṣaṇam /
snigdhaṃ kuntalasaṃbhinnakirīṭavanamālinam //
1.80.d:
उन्निद्रेदीवरश्यामं पद्मपत्रायतेक्षणम् ।
स्निग्धं कुन्तलसंभिन्नकिरीटवनमालिनम् ॥
1.80.m:
dark like a blooming blue lotus, with long eyes like lotus petals,
sleek, wearing a crown intermingled with locks of hair, and wearing a woodland garland;

1.80.s:
cāruprasannavadanaṃ sphuranmakarakuṇḍalam /
śrīvatsavakṣasaṃ bhrājatkaustubhaṃ sumanoharam //
1.80.d:
चारुप्रसन्नवदनं स्फुरन्मकरकुण्डलम् ।
श्रीवत्सवक्षसं भ्राजत्कौस्तुभं सुमनोहरम् ॥
1.80.m:
with a lovely, serene face, with glittering alligator-shaped earrings,
with the Śrīvatsa on his chest, with the shining Kaustubha gem, enchanting the mind;

1.80.s:
kāśmīrakapiśoraskaṃ pītakauśeyavāsasam /
hārakeyūrakaṭakakaṭisūtrairalaṅkṛtam //
1.80.d:
काश्मीरकपिशोरस्कं पीतकौशेयवाससम् ।
हारकेयूरकटककटिसूत्रैरलङ्कृतम् ॥
1.80.m:
whose chest is tawny with saffron, who wears yellow silk garments,
adorned with necklaces, armlets, bracelets, and a waist-cord;

1.80.s:
hṛtaviśvaṃbharābhūribhāraṃ muditamānasam /
śaṅkhacakragadāpadmarājadbhujacatuṣṭayam //
1.80.d:
हृतविश्वंभराभूरिभारं मुदितमानसम् ।
शङ्खचक्रगदापद्मराजद्भुजचतुष्टयम् ॥
1.80.m:
who has removed the heavy burden of the earth, joyful at heart,
whose four arms shine with the conch, discus, club, and lotus.

1.80.s:
evaṃ dhyātvārcayenmantrī syādaṅgaiḥ prathamāvṛttiḥ /
dvitīyā mahiṣībhistu tṛtīyāyāṃ samarcayet //
1.80.d:
एवं ध्यात्वार्चयेन्मन्त्री स्यादङ्गैः प्रथमावृत्तिः ।
द्वितीया महिषीभिस्तु तृतीयायां समर्चयेत् ॥
1.80.m:
Having meditated thus, the practitioner of mantras should worship. The first circuit should consist of the [six] limbs;
the second, however, of his chief queens; in the third, he should worship

1.80.s:
nāradaṃ parvataṃ jiṣṇuṃ niśaṭhoddhavadārukān /
viṣvaksenaṃ ca śaineyaṃ dikṣvagre vinatāsutam //
1.80.d:
नारदं पर्वतं जिष्णुं निशठोद्धवदारुकान् ।
विष्वक्सेनं च शैनेयं दिक्ष्वग्रे विनतासुतम् ॥
1.80.m:
Nārada, Parvata, Arjuna, Niśaṭha, Uddhava, and Dāruka,
as well as Viṣvaksena and Sātyaki in the directions, and the son of Vinatā in front.

1.80.s:
lokapālaiśca vajrādyaiḥ pūjayedvaiṣṇavottamaḥ /
evaṃ saṃpūjya vidhivatpāyasaṃ vinivedayet //
1.80.d:
लोकपालैश्च वज्राद्यैः पूजयेद्वैष्णवोत्तमः ।
एवं संपूज्य विधिवत्पायसं विनिवेदयेत् ॥
1.80.m:
The best of Vaiṣṇavas should worship [the fourth circuit] with the world-protectors and their weapons such as the thunderbolt.
Having thus worshipped according to rule, he should offer milk-rice.

1.80.s:
tarpayitvā khaṇḍamiśradugdhabuddhyā jalairiha /
japedaṣṭaśataṃ mantrī bhāvayanpuruṣottamam //
1.80.d:
तर्पयित्वा खण्डमिश्रदुग्धबुद्ध्या जलैरिह ।
जपेदष्टशतं मन्त्री भावयन्पुरुषोत्तमम् ॥
1.80.m:
Having offered water-gratification here with water considered to be milk mixed with candied sugar,
the practitioner of mantras should recite [the mantra] one hundred and eight times, meditating on the Supreme Person.

1.80.s:
pūjāsu homaṃ sarvāsu kuryānmadhyandine 'thavā /
āsanādarghyaparyantaṃ kṛtvā stutvā nametsudhīḥ //
1.80.d:
पूजासु होमं सर्वासु कुर्यान्मध्यन्दिने ऽथवा ।
आसनादर्घ्यपर्यन्तं कृत्वा स्तुत्वा नमेत्सुधीः ॥
1.80.m:
In all these acts of worship, or at midday, one should perform a fire oblation.
Having performed [the rites] from the seat up to the water offering, the wise person should praise and bow down.

1.80.s:
samarthātmānamudvāsya svīyahṛtsarasīruhe /
vinyasya tanmayo bhūtvā punarātmānamarcayet //
1.80.d:
समर्थात्मानमुद्वास्य स्वीयहृत्सरसीरुहे ।
विन्यस्य तन्मयो भूत्वा पुनरात्मानमर्चयेत् ॥
1.80.m: Bidding farewell to the deity, and establishing him, fully capable, / within the lotus of his own heart, becoming one with him, he should again worship himself.

1.80.s:
sāyāhne vāsudevaṃ yo nityamevaṃ samarcayet /
sarvānkāmānavāpyānte sa yāti paramāṃ gatim //
1.80.d:
सायाह्ने वासुदेवं यो नित्यमेवं समर्चयेत् ।
सर्वान्कामानवाप्यान्ते स याति परमां गतिम् ॥
1.80.m:
He who always worships Vāsudeva thus in the evening,
having attained all desires, goes in the end to the supreme goal.

1.80.s:
rātrau cenmadanākrāntacetasaṃ nandanandanam /
yajedrāsapariśrāntaṃ gopīmaṇḍalamadhyagam //
1.80.d:
रात्रौ चेन्मदनाक्रान्तचेतसं नन्दनन्दनम् ।
यजेद्रासपरिश्रान्तं गोपीमण्डलमध्यगम् ॥
1.80.m:
If at night, one should worship the son of Nanda whose heart is overcome with passion,
fatigued by the rāsa dance, standing in the midst of the circle of cowherdesses,

1.80.s:
vikasatkundakahlāramallikākusumodgataiḥ /
rajobhirdhūsarairmandamārutaiḥ śiśirīkṛte //
1.80.d:
विकसत्कुन्दकह्लारमल्लिकाकुसुमोद्गतैः ।
रजोभिर्धूसरैर्मन्दमारुतैः शिशिरीकृते ॥
1.80.m:
made cool by gentle breezes gray with the pollen
arising from the blossoms of blooming kunda, kahlāra, and mallikā jasmines,

1.80.s:
unmīlannavakairavālivigalanmādhvīkalabdhāntaraṃ bhrāmyanmattamilindagītalalite sanmallikojjṛmbhite /
pīyūṣāṃśukarairviśālitaharitprānte smaroddīpane kālindīpulināṅgaṇe smitamukhaṃ veṇuṃ raṇantaṃ muhuḥ //
1.80.d:
उन्मीलन्नवकैरवालिविगलन्माध्वीकलब्धान्तरं भ्राम्यन्मत्तमिलिन्दगीतललिते सन्मल्लिकोज्जृम्भिते ।
पीयूषांशुकरैर्विशालितहरित्प्रान्ते स्मरोद्दीपने कालिन्दीपुलिनाङ्गणे स्मितमुखं वेणुं रणन्तं मुहुः ॥
1.80.m:
in an open courtyard on the bank of the Yamunā that inflames desire, where the directions are expanded by the nectar-rays [of the moon],
blossoming with fine mallikā jasmines, charming with the songs of intoxicated bees wandering into the openings of the dripping nectar of rows of blooming fresh night-lotuses, smiling-faced, repeatedly sounding the flute,

1.80.s:
antastoyalasannavāṃbudaghaṭāsaṃghaṭṭakāratviṣaṃ cañcañcillikamaṃbujāyatadṛśaṃ bimbādharaṃ sundaram /
māyūracchadabaddhamaulivilasaddhaṃmillamālaṃ calaṃ dīpyatkuṇḍalaratnaraśmivilasadgaṇḍadvayodbāsitam //
1.80.d:
अन्तस्तोयलसन्नवांबुदघटासंघट्टकारत्विषं चञ्चञ्चिल्लिकमंबुजायतदृशं बिम्बाधरं सुन्दरम् ।
मायूरच्छदबद्धमौलिविलसद्धंमिल्लमालं चलं दीप्यत्कुण्डलरत्नरश्मिविलसद्गण्डद्वयोद्बासितम् ॥
1.80.m:
having the luster of an array of fresh water-bearing rainclouds, with dancing eyebrows, long lotus eyes, and bimba-fruit lips, handsome,
with a garland entwined in his braided hair on his head crowned with peacock feathers, moving, illuminated by his two cheeks radiant with the gems of his glittering earrings,

1.80.s:
kāñcīnūpurahārakaṅkaṇalasatkeyūrabhūṣānvitaṃ gopīnāṃ dvitayāṃ tare sulalitaṃ vanyaprasūnasrajam /
anyonyaṃ vinibaddhagopadayitādorvallivītaṃ lasadrāsakrīḍanalolupaṃ manasijākrāntaṃ mukundaṃ bhavet //
1.80.d:
काञ्चीनूपुरहारकङ्कणलसत्केयूरभूषान्वितं गोपीनां द्वितयां तरे सुललितं वन्यप्रसूनस्रजम् ।
अन्योन्यं विनिबद्धगोपदयितादोर्वल्लिवीतं लसद्रासक्रीडनलोलुपं मनसिजाक्रान्तं मुकुन्दं भवेत् ॥
1.80.m:
endowed with ornaments of girdles, anklets, necklaces, bracelets, and gleaming armlets, graceful between pairs of cowherdesses, wearing a garland of forest flowers,
embraced by the creeper-like arms of the beloved cowherdesses linked together, Mukunda, eager for the splendid rāsa dance, overcome by love, should be [meditated upon]:

1.80.s:
vividhaśrutibhinnamanojñatarasvarasaptakamūrchanatānagaṇaiḥ /
bhramamāṇamamūbhirudāramaṇisphuṭamaṇḍanasiṃjitacārutanum //
1.80.d:
विविधश्रुतिभिन्नमनोज्ञतरस्वरसप्तकमूर्छनतानगणैः ।
भ्रममाणममूभिरुदारमणिस्फुटमण्डनसिंजितचारुतनुम् ॥
1.80.m:
moving about with them through hosts of musical pauses and melodic expansions of the seven charming notes differentiated by various microtones,
his lovely body tinkling with clear ornaments of noble jewels;

1.80.s:
itaretarabaddhakarapramadāgaṇakalpitarāsavihāravidhau /
maṇiśaṅkugamapyamunā vapuṣā bahudhā vihitasvakadivyatanum //
1.80.d:
इतरेतरबद्धकरप्रमदागणकल्पितरासविहारविधौ ।
मणिशङ्कुगमप्यमुना वपुषा बहुधा विहितस्वकदिव्यतनुम् ॥
1.80.m:
in the performance of the rāsa play devised by the throngs of women who held each other's hands,
though he stood at the jeweled post, he multiplied his divine body into many through that very form.

1.80.s:
evaṃ dhyātvārcayenmantrī syādaṅgaiḥ prathamāvṛtiḥ /
śrīkāmaḥ sasvarādyāni kalābjairvaiṣṇavottamaḥ //
1.80.d:
एवं ध्यात्वार्चयेन्मन्त्री स्यादङ्गैः प्रथमावृतिः ।
श्रीकामः सस्वराद्यानि कलाब्जैर्वैष्णवोत्तमः ॥
1.80.m:
Having meditated thus, the practitioner of mantras should worship. The first circuit should consist of the [six] limbs.
Desiring prosperity, the best of Vaiṣṇavas, with the lotuses of parts starting with the vowels,

1.80.s:
yajetkeśavakīrtyādimithunāni ca ṣoḍaśa /
indrādyānapi vajrādīnpūjayettadanantaram //
1.80.d:
यजेत्केशवकीर्त्यादिमिथुनानि च षोडश ।
इन्द्राद्यानपि वज्रादीन्पूजयेत्तदनन्तरम् ॥
1.80.m:
should worship the sixteen pairs beginning with Keśava and Kīrti;
and immediately after that, he should worship Indra and the others, as well as the thunderbolt and the other [weapons].

1.80.s:
pṛnthu suvṛttaṃ masṛṇaṃ vitastimātronnataṃ kau vinikhanya śaṅkum /
ākramya padbhyāmitaretaraistu hastairbhramo 'yaṃ khalu rāsagoṣṭhī //
1.80.d:
पृन्थु सुवृत्तं मसृणं वितस्तिमात्रोन्नतं कौ विनिखन्य शङ्कुम् ।
आक्रम्य पद्भ्यामितरेतरैस्तु हस्तैर्भ्रमो ऽयं खलु रासगोष्ठी ॥
1.80.m:
Having driven into the ground a thick, well-rounded, smooth peg only a span in height,
pressing it with their feet while holding hands with one another, this circling is indeed the gathering of the rāsa.

1.80.s:
sapūjyaivaṃ ca payasā sasito palasarpiṣā /
naivedyamarcayitvā tu caṣakairnṛpasaṃkhyakaiḥ //
1.80.d:
सपूज्यैवं च पयसा ससितो पलसर्पिषा ।
नैवेद्यमर्चयित्वा तु चषकैर्नृपसंख्यकैः ॥
1.80.m:
Having thus worshipped, and having offered an oblation of food with milk, sugar-candy, and ghee
using sixteen cups,

1.80.s:
satataṃ pāpapte (?) mantrī mithuneṣvarpayetkramāt /
vidhāya pūrvavaccheṣaṃ sahasraṃ prajapenmanum //
1.80.d:
सततं पापप्ते (?) मन्त्री मिथुनेष्वर्पयेत्क्रमात् ।
विधाय पूर्ववच्छेषं सहस्रं प्रजपेन्मनुम् ॥
1.80.m:
the practitioner of mantras should continuously offer […] to the pairs in order;
having performed the remainder as before, he should recite the mantra a thousand times.

1.80.s:
stutvā natvā ca saṃprārthya pūjāśeṣaṃ samāpayet /
evaṃ yaḥ pūjayetkṛṣṇaṃ sa sasmṛddheḥ padaṃ bhavet //
1.80.d:
स्तुत्वा नत्वा च संप्रार्थ्य पूजाशेषं समापयेत् ।
एवं यः पूजयेत्कृष्णं स सस्मृद्धेः पदं भवेत् ॥
1.80.m:
Having praised, bowed, and prayed, he should complete the conclusion of the worship.
He who thus worships Kṛṣṇa becomes an abode of prosperity.

1.80.s:
aṇimādyaṣṭasiddhīnāmīśvaraḥ syānna saṃśayaḥ /
bhuktveha vividhānbhogānante viṣṇupadaṃ vrajet //
1.80.d:
अणिमाद्यष्टसिद्धीनामीश्वरः स्यान्न संशयः ।
भुक्त्वेह विविधान्भोगानन्ते विष्णुपदं व्रजेत् ॥
1.80.m: He will become a master of the eight supernatural powers such as atomicity, there is no doubt; / having enjoyed various delights in this world, he will go at the end to the realm of Viṣṇu.

1.80.s:
evaṃ pūjādibhiḥ siddhe manaukāmyāni sādhayet /
aṣṭāviṃśativāraṃ vā trikālaṃ pūjayetsudhīḥ //
1.80.d:
एवं पूजादिभिः सिद्धे मनौकाम्यानि साधयेत् ।
अष्टाविंशतिवारं वा त्रिकालं पूजयेत्सुधीः ॥
1.80.m: Once the mantra has been thus mastered by worship and the like, he may accomplish his desired ends; / or the wise practitioner should worship three times a day, twenty-eight times [each].

1.80.s:
svakālavihitān bhūyaḥ parivārāṃśca tarpayet /
prātarddadhnā guḍāktena madhyāhne payasā punaḥ //
1.80.d:
स्वकालविहितान् भूयः परिवारांश्च तर्पयेत् ।
प्रातर्द्दध्ना गुडाक्तेन मध्याह्ने पयसा पुनः ॥
1.80.m: He should again offer water-oblations to the retinue prescribed for their proper times: / in the morning with curd mixed with jaggery, and at midday with milk;

1.80.s:
navanītayutenātha sāyāhne tarpayetpunaḥ /
sasitopalamiśreṇa payasā vaiṣṇavottamaḥ //
1.80.d:
नवनीतयुतेनाथ सायाह्ने तर्पयेत्पुनः ।
ससितोपलमिश्रेण पयसा वैष्णवोत्तमः ॥
1.80.m: then in the evening, the best of Vaiṣṇavas / should again offer water-oblations with milk mixed with fresh butter and rock sugar.

1.80.s:
tarpayāmipadaṃ yojyaṃ mantrānte sveṣu nāmasu /
dvitīyānteṣu tu punaḥ pūjāśeṣaṃ samāpayet //
1.80.d:
तर्पयामिपदं योज्यं मन्त्रान्ते स्वेषु नामसु ।
द्वितीयान्तेषु तु पुनः पूजाशेषं समापयेत् ॥
1.80.m: The word ‘tarpayāmi’ should be joined at the end of the mantra to his own names / in the accusative case; and then he should conclude the remainder of the worship.

1.80.s:
abhyukṣyatatprasādādbhirātmānaṃ prapabedapaḥ /
tattṛtpastamathodvāsya tanmayaḥ prajapenmanum //
1.80.d:
अभ्युक्ष्यतत्प्रसादाद्भिरात्मानं प्रपबेदपः ।
तत्तृत्पस्तमथोद्वास्य तन्मयः प्रजपेन्मनुम् ॥
1.80.m: Sprinkling himself with the water of His prasāda, he should drink that water; / satisfied by it, having then dismissed Him, absorbed in Him, he should recite the mantra.

1.80.s:
atha dravyāṇi kāmyeṣu procyante tarpaṇeṣu ca /
tāni proktavidhānānāmāśrityānyatamaṃ bhajet //
1.80.d:
अथ द्रव्याणि काम्येषु प्रोच्यन्ते तर्पणेषु च ।
तानि प्रोक्तविधानानामाश्रित्यान्यतमं भजेत् ॥
1.80.m: Now the substances used in desire-prompted rites and water-oblations are declared; / having resorted to any one of these prescribed offerings, he should worship:

1.80.s:
pāyasaṃ dādhikaṃ cājyaṃ gauḍānnaṃ kṛsaraṃ payaḥ /
dadhīni kadalī mocā ciñcā rajasvalā tathā //
1.80.d:
पायसं दाधिकं चाज्यं गौडान्नं कृसरं पयः ।
दधीनि कदली मोचा चिञ्चा रजस्वला तथा ॥
1.80.m: Rice-pudding, curd-rice, clarified butter, molasses-rice, spiced rice-and-lentil mash, milk, / curds, plantain, banana, tamarind, and the citrus fruit,

1.80.s:
apūpā modakā lājāḥ pṛthukā navanītakam /
dravyaṣoḍaśakaṃ hyetatkathitaṃ padmajādibhiḥ //
1.80.d:
अपूपा मोदका लाजाः पृथुका नवनीतकम् ।
द्रव्यषोडशकं ह्येतत्कथितं पद्मजादिभिः ॥
1.80.m: sweet cakes, round sweets, parched grains, flattened rice, and fresh butter: / these sixteen substances have indeed been declared by the lotus-born Brahmā and others.

1.80.s:
lājānte pṛthukaṃ prākca samarpya ca sitopalam /
catuḥsaptativāraṃ yaḥ prātarevaṃ pratarpayet //
1.80.d:
लाजान्ते पृथुकं प्राक्च समर्प्य च सितोपलम् ।
चतुःसप्ततिवारं यः प्रातरेवं प्रतर्पयेत् ॥
1.80.m: Having offered flattened rice after parched grains, and rock sugar before, / he who thus offers water-oblations seventy-four times in the morning,

1.80.s:
dhyātvā kṛṣṇapadaṃ matrī maṇḍalādiṣṭamāpnuyāt /
dhāroṣṇapakkapayasā navanītaṃ dadhīni ca //
1.80.d:
ध्यात्वा कृष्णपदं मत्री मण्डलादिष्टमाप्नुयात् ।
धारोष्णपक्कपयसा नवनीतं दधीनि च ॥
1.80.m: meditating on the feet of Kṛṣṇa, the mantrin will attain his desire within forty days. / With milk warm from the udder and boiled milk, fresh butter, curds,

1.80.s:
daugdhāmrāmājyaṃ matsyaṇḍī kṣaudraṃ kīlālameva ca /
pūjayennavabhirdravyaiḥ pratyekaṃ ravisaṃkhyayā //
1.80.d:
दौग्धाम्रामाज्यं मत्स्यण्डी क्षौद्रं कीलालमेव च ।
पूजयेन्नवभिर्द्रव्यैः प्रत्येकं रविसंख्यया ॥
1.80.m: milky mango, clarified butter, candied sugar, honey, and water: / he should worship with these nine substances, each twelve times in number.

1.80.s:
evamaṣṭotaraśataṃsaṃkhyākaṃ tarpaṇaṃ punaḥ /
yaḥ kuryādvaiṣṇavaśreṣṭhaḥ pūrvoktaṃ phalamāpnuyāt //
1.80.d:
एवमष्टोतरशतंसंख्याकं तर्पणं पुनः ।
यः कुर्याद्वैष्णवश्रेष्ठः पूर्वोक्तं फलमाप्नुयात् ॥
1.80.m: Whoever, the best of Vaiṣṇavas, thus performs a water-oblation / numbering one hundred and eight times, attains the fruit stated previously.

1.80.s:
kiṃ bahūktena sarveṣṭadāyakaṃ tarpaṇaṃ tvidam /
sasitopaladhāroṣṇadugdhabuddhyā jalena vai //
1.80.d:
किं बहूक्तेन सर्वेष्टदायकं तर्पणं त्विदम् ।
ससितोपलधारोष्णदुग्धबुद्ध्या जलेन वै ॥
1.80.m: What need of saying much? This water-oblation bestows all desires: / by using water with the mental conception of milk warm from the udder mixed with rock sugar,

1.80.s:
kṛṣṇaṃ prataparyan grāmaṃ vrajanprāpnoti sādhakaḥ /
dhanavastrāṇi bhojyaṃ ca parivāragaṇaiḥ saha //
1.80.d:
कृष्णं प्रतपर्यन् ग्रामं व्रजन्प्राप्नोति साधकः ।
धनवस्त्राणि भोज्यं च परिवारगणैः सह ॥
1.80.m: a practitioner offering water-oblations to Kṛṣṇa while going to a village obtains / wealth, garments, food, and a retinue of attendants.

1.80.s:
yāvatsaṃtarpayenmantrī tāvatsaṃkhyaṃ japenmanum /
tarpaṇenaiva kāryāṇi sādhayedakhilānyapi //
1.80.d:
यावत्संतर्पयेन्मन्त्री तावत्संख्यं जपेन्मनुम् ।
तर्पणेनैव कार्याणि साधयेदखिलान्यपि ॥
1.80.m: As many times as the mantrin offers water-oblations, so many times he should recite the mantra; / by the water-oblation alone he can accomplish all undertakings.

1.80.s:
kāmyahomamatho vakṣye sādhakānāṃ hitāya ca /
śrīpuṣpairjuhuyānmantrī śriyamicchannininditām //
1.80.d:
काम्यहोममथो वक्ष्ये साधकानां हिताय च ।
श्रीपुष्पैर्जुहुयान्मन्त्री श्रियमिच्छन्निनिन्दिताम् ॥
1.80.m: Now I shall declare the desire-prompted fire oblation for the welfare of practitioners: / the mantrin desiring unblemished fortune should offer oblations of lotus flowers.

1.80.s:
sājyenānnena juhuyātghṛtānnasya samṛddhaye /
vanyapuṣpairdvijān jātīpuṣpaiśca pṛthivīpatīn //
1.80.d:
साज्येनान्नेन जुहुयात्घृतान्नस्य समृद्धये ।
वन्यपुष्पैर्द्विजान् जातीपुष्पैश्च पृथिवीपतीन् ॥
1.80.m: He should offer food mixed with clarified butter to obtain an abundance of food cooked in ghee; / he subjugates twice-born people with wild flowers, and kings with jasmine flowers,

1.80.s:
asitaiḥ kusumairvaiśyān śūdrānnīlotpalaistathā /
vaśayellavaṇaiḥ sarvānaṃbujairyuvatījanam //
1.80.d:
असितैः कुसुमैर्वैश्यान् शूद्रान्नीलोत्पलैस्तथा ।
वशयेल्लवणैः सर्वानंबुजैर्युवतीजनम् ॥
1.80.m: vaiśyas with dark flowers, and śūdras with blue water-lilies; / he can subjugate all people with salts, and young women with lotuses.

1.80.s:
gośālāsu kṛto homaḥ pāyasena sasarpiṣā /
gavāṃ śāntiṃ karotyāśu gopālo gokuleśvaraḥ //
1.80.d:
गोशालासु कृतो होमः पायसेन ससर्पिषा ।
गवां शान्तिं करोत्याशु गोपालो गोकुलेश्वरः ॥
1.80.m: A fire oblation performed in cowsheds with rice-pudding mixed with clarified butter / quickly brings peace to the cows, through Gopāla, the Lord of Gokula.

1.80.s:
śikṣāveṣadharaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ kiṅkiṇījālaśobhitam /
dhyātvā pratarpayenmantrī dugdhabuddhyā śubhairjalaiḥ //
1.80.d:
शिक्षावेषधरं कृष्णं किङ्किणीजालशोभितम् ।
ध्यात्वा प्रतर्पयेन्मन्त्री दुग्धबुद्ध्या शुभैर्जलैः ॥
1.80.m: Meditating on Kṛṣṇa dressed as a pupil and adorned with a network of jingling bells, / the mantrin should offer water-oblations with pure waters, with the mental conception of milk.

1.80.s:
dhanaṃ dhānyaṃ sutānkīrtiṃ prītastasmai dadāti saḥ /
brahmavṛkṣasamidbhirvā kuśairvā tilatandulaiḥ //
1.80.d:
धनं धान्यं सुतान्कीर्तिं प्रीतस्तस्मै ददाति सः ।
ब्रह्मवृक्षसमिद्भिर्वा कुशैर्वा तिलतन्दुलैः ॥
1.80.m: Pleased, He bestows upon him wealth, grain, sons, and renown. / Or with fuel-sticks of the palāśa tree, with kuśa grass, or with sesame and rice grains,

1.80.s:
juhuyādayutaṃ mantrī trimadhvāktairhutāśane /
vaśaye dbrāhmaṇāṃścātha rājavṛkṣasamudbhavaiḥ //
1.80.d:
जुहुयादयुतं मन्त्री त्रिमध्वाक्तैर्हुताशने ।
वशये द्ब्राह्मणांश्चाथ राजवृक्षसमुद्भवैः ॥
1.80.m: the mantrin should offer ten thousand oblations into the fire, smeared with the three sweets. / Then he can subjugate brāhmaṇas; and with blossoms originating from the aragvadha tree

1.80.s:
prasūnaiḥ kṣatriyānvaiśyānkuraṇḍakusumaistathā /
pāṭalotthaiśca kusumairvaśayedantimānsudhīḥ //
1.80.d:
प्रसूनैः क्षत्रियान्वैश्यान्कुरण्डकुसुमैस्तथा ।
पाटलोत्थैश्च कुसुमैर्वशयेदन्तिमान्सुधीः ॥
1.80.m: he subjugates kṣatriyas, and vaiśyas with yellow amaranth flowers; / and the wise one can subjugate the lowest class with flowers born of the trumpet-flower tree.

1.80.s:
śvetapadmai raktapapdaiścaṃpakaiḥ pāṭalaiḥ kramāt /
hutvāyutaṃ trimadhvāktairvaśayettadvarāṅganāḥ //
1.80.d:
श्वेतपद्मै रक्तपप्दैश्चंपकैः पाटलैः क्रमात् ।
हुत्वायुतं त्रिमध्वाक्तैर्वशयेत्तद्वराङ्गनाः ॥
1.80.m: Having offered ten thousand oblations smeared with the three sweets with white lotuses, / red lotuses, campaka blossoms, and trumpet-flowers in turn, he can subjugate their noble women.

1.80.s:
nityaṃ hayārikusumaurniśīthe trimadhuplutaiḥ /
varastrīrvaśayetprājñaḥ samyagdhṛtvā dināṣṭakam //
1.80.d:
नित्यं हयारिकुसुमौर्निशीथे त्रिमधुप्लुतैः ।
वरस्त्रीर्वशयेत्प्राज्ञः सम्यग्धृत्वा दिनाष्टकम् ॥
1.80.m: Constantly offering at midnight oleander flowers submerged in the three sweets, / the wise man can subjugate noble women after maintaining it fully for eight days.

1.80.s:
ayutatritayaṃ rātrau siddhārthaistrimadhuplutaiḥ /
pratyahaṃ juhvato māsātsureśo 'pi vaśībhavet //
1.80.d:
अयुतत्रितयं रात्रौ सिद्धार्थैस्त्रिमधुप्लुतैः ।
प्रत्यहं जुह्वतो मासात्सुरेशो ऽपि वशीभवेत् ॥
1.80.m: If one offers thirty thousand oblations at night with white mustard seeds soaked in the three sweets / every day for a month, even the lord of the gods is brought under subjugation.

1.80.s:
āhṛtya ballavīvastrāṇyārūḍhaṃ nīpabhūruhe /
smaretkṛṣṇaṃ japedrātrau sahasraṃ khendūhātsudhīḥ //
1.80.d:
आहृत्य बल्लवीवस्त्राण्यारूढं नीपभूरुहे ।
स्मरेत्कृष्णं जपेद्रात्रौ सहस्रं खेन्दूहात्सुधीः ॥
1.80.m: Having taken the clothes of the cowherd women, mounted upon a kadamba tree— / the wise one should remember Kṛṣṇa thus and recite at night a thousand times for one month;

1.80.s:
haṭhādākarṣayecchīghramurvaśīmapi sādhakaḥ /
bahunā kimihoktena mantro 'yaṃ sarvavaśyakṛt //
1.80.d:
हठादाकर्षयेच्छीघ्रमुर्वशीमपि साधकः ।
बहुना किमिहोक्तेन मन्त्रो ऽयं सर्ववश्यकृत् ॥
1.80.m: the practitioner can forcibly and quickly attract even Urvaśī. / What need is there of saying much here? This mantra brings all under subjugation.

1.80.s:
rahasyaṃ paramaṃ cātha vakṣye mokṣapradaṃ nṛṇām /
dhyāyetsvahṛtsarasije devakīnandanaṃ vibhum //
1.80.d:
रहस्यं परमं चाथ वक्ष्ये मोक्षप्रदं नृणाम् ।
ध्यायेत्स्वहृत्सरसिजे देवकीनन्दनं विभुम् ॥
1.80.m: And now I shall declare the supreme secret that grants liberation to men: / one should meditate on the all-pervading Son of Devakī in the lotus of one's heart.

1.80.s:
śrīmatkundendugauraṃ sarasijanayanaṃ śaṅkhacakre gadābje bibhrāṇaṃ hastapadmairnavanalinalasanmālayādīpyamānam /
vande vedyaṃ munīndraiḥ kaṇikamunilasaddivyabhūṣābhirāmaṃ divyāṅgālepabhāsaṃ sakalabhayaharaṃ pītavastraṃ nurārim //
1.80.d:
श्रीमत्कुन्देन्दुगौरं सरसिजनयनं शङ्खचक्रे गदाब्जे बिभ्राणं हस्तपद्मैर्नवनलिनलसन्मालयादीप्यमानम् ।
वन्दे वेद्यं मुनीन्द्रैः कणिकमुनिलसद्दिव्यभूषाभिरामं दिव्याङ्गालेपभासं सकलभयहरं पीतवस्त्रं नुरारिम् ॥
1.80.m: I praise the foe of Mura, white as the beauteous kunda flower and moon, with lotus eyes, bearing the conch, discus, mace, and lotus / in his lotus hands, shining with a garland of fresh lotuses, / to be known by the chief sages, charming with gleaming divine ornaments of fine gems, / radiant with divine unguents on his limbs, dispelling all fear, clad in yellow garments.

1.80.s:
evaṃ dhyātvā pumāṃsaṃ sphuṭahṛdayasarojāsanāsīnamādyaṃ sāṃdrāṃbhodācchabiṃbādbhutakanakanibhaṃ saṃjapedarkalakṣam /
manvorekaṃ dvitārāntaritamathaḥ hunedarkasāhasramidhmaiḥ kṣīridrūttharyathoktaiḥ samadhughṛtasitenāthavā pāyasena //
1.80.d:
एवं ध्यात्वा पुमांसं स्फुटहृदयसरोजासनासीनमाद्यं सांद्रांभोदाच्छबिंबाद्भुतकनकनिभं संजपेदर्कलक्षम् ।
मन्वोरेकं द्वितारान्तरितमथः हुनेदर्कसाहस्रमिध्मैः क्षीरिद्रूत्थर्यथोक्तैः समधुघृतसितेनाथवा पायसेन ॥
1.80.m: Having thus meditated on the Primordial Person seated on the expanded lotus-throne of the heart, / resembling pure gold within a dense cloud-circle, he should recite twelve hundred thousand times / one of the two mantras, intercalated with two tāra syllables; then he should offer twelve thousand oblations with fuel-sticks / from milk-yielding trees as prescribed, or with milk-pudding mixed with honey, clarified butter, and sugar.

1.80.s:
evaṃ lokeśvarārādhyaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ svahṛdayāṃbuje /
dhyāyannanudinaṃ mantrī trisahasraṃ japenmanum //
1.80.d:
एवं लोकेश्वराराध्यं कृष्णं स्वहृदयांबुजे ।
ध्यायन्ननुदिनं मन्त्री त्रिसहस्रं जपेन्मनुम् ॥
1.80.m: Thus meditating in the lotus of his own heart upon Kṛṣṇa, who is worshipped by the Lord of the world, / the mantrin should recite the mantra three thousand times every day.

1.80.s:
sāyāhnoktena vidhinā saṃpūjya havanaṃ punaḥ /
kṛtvā pūrvoktavidhinā mantrī tadgatamānasaḥ //
1.80.d:
सायाह्नोक्तेन विधिना संपूज्य हवनं पुनः ।
कृत्वा पूर्वोक्तविधिना मन्त्री तद्गतमानसः ॥
1.80.m: Having worshipped according to the rule prescribed for the evening, and again performing a fire oblation / according to the previously stated rule, the mantrin, with his mind fixed on Him,

1.80.s:
evaṃ yo bhajate nityaṃ vidvān gopālanandanam /
samuttīrya bhavāṃbhodhiṃ sa yāti paramaṃ padam //
1.80.d:
एवं यो भजते नित्यं विद्वान् गोपालनन्दनम् ।
समुत्तीर्य भवांभोधिं स याति परमं पदम् ॥
1.80.m: the learned man who thus continually worships the Delight of Gopāla, / crossing over the ocean of worldly existence, goes to the supreme abode.

1.80.s:
madhye keṇeṣu bāhyeṣvanalapurapuṭasyālikhetkarṇikāyāṃ kandarpaṃ sādhyayuktaṃ vivaragataṣaḍarṇadviṣaḥ keśareṣu /
śaktiḥ śrīpūrvikāṇidvinavalipimanorakṣarāṇicchadānāṃ madhye varṇāndaśānto daśalipimanuvaryasya vaikaikaśo 'bjam //
1.80.d:
मध्ये केणेषु बाह्येष्वनलपुरपुटस्यालिखेत्कर्णिकायां कन्दर्पं साध्ययुक्तं विवरगतषडर्णद्विषः केशरेषु ।
शक्तिः श्रीपूर्विकाणिद्विनवलिपिमनोरक्षराणिच्छदानां मध्ये वर्णान्दशान्तो दशलिपिमनुवर्यस्य वैकैकशो ऽब्जम् ॥
1.80.m: In the center, in the corners, and outside the fold of the fire-city, in the pericarp, one should write / the god of love together with the name of the person to be influenced; in the intervals, the six-syllabled foe [syllables]; on the filaments, / the Śakti and Śrī seed-syllables; and on the petals, one should write the letters of the eighteen-syllabled mantra / or the letters of the excellent ten-syllabled mantra, one by one, on the lotus, with the ten-syllabled ending.

1.80.s:
bhūsadmanābhivṛtamasragamanmathena gorocanāvilikhitaṃ tapanīyasūcyā /
paṭṭe hiraṇyaracite gulikīkṛtaṃ tadgopālayantramakhilārthadametaduktam //
1.80.d:
भूसद्मनाभिवृतमस्रगमन्मथेन गोरोचनाविलिखितं तपनीयसूच्या ।
पट्टे हिरण्यरचिते गुलिकीकृतं तद्गोपालयन्त्रमखिलार्थदमेतदुक्तम् ॥
1.80.m: Enclosed by an earth-abode, angled, accompanied by Kāma, drawn with yellow pigment using a golden needle, / rolled into a talisman on a plate made of gold—this is declared to be the Gopāla yantra that bestows all ends.

1.80.s:
saṃyātasiktamabhijaptamimaṃ mahadbhirdhāryaṃ jagattrayavaśīkaraṇaikadakṣam /
rakṣāyaśaḥ sutamahīdhanadhānyalakṣmīsaubhāgyalipsubhirajasramanarghyavīryam //
1.80.d:
संयातसिक्तमभिजप्तमिमं महद्भिर्धार्यं जगत्त्रयवशीकरणैकदक्षम् ।
रक्षायशः सुतमहीधनधान्यलक्ष्मीसौभाग्यलिप्सुभिरजस्रमनर्घ्यवीर्यम् ॥
1.80.m: Consecrated and repeatedly chanted over by great souls, this should be worn as it is uniquely skilled in subjugating the three worlds, / possessing priceless power, constantly by those desiring protection, fame, sons, earth, wealth, grain, fortune, and prosperity.

1.80.s:
smarastrivikramākrāntaścākrīṣṭyāya hṛdityasau /
ṣaḍakṣaro 'yaṃ saṃproktaḥ sarvasiddhikaro manuḥ //
1.80.d:
स्मरस्त्रिविक्रमाक्रान्तश्चाक्रीष्ट्याय हृदित्यसौ ।
षडक्षरो ऽयं संप्रोक्तः सर्वसिद्धिकरो मनुः ॥
1.80.m: ‘Smara’ followed by ‘Trivikrama’, ‘Cākrin’, ‘iṣṭi’, and ‘hṛd’— / this is declared to be the six-syllabled mantra that brings about all accomplishments.

1.80.s:
kroḍaḥ śāntīnduvahnyāḍhyo māyā bīja prakīrtatam /
govindavahnicandrāḍhyo manuḥ śrībījamīritam //
1.80.d:
क्रोडः शान्तीन्दुवह्न्याढ्यो माया बीज प्रकीर्ततम् ।
गोविन्दवह्निचन्द्राढ्यो मनुः श्रीबीजमीरितम् ॥
1.80.m: ‘Kroḍa’ endowed with ‘śānti’, moon, and fire is proclaimed as the māyābīja; / the mantra endowed with ‘Govinda’, fire, and moon is spoken of as the śrībīja.

1.80.s:
ābhyāmaṣṭādaśaklipaḥ syādviṃśatyakṣaro manuḥ /
śālagrāme maṇau yantre maṇḍale pratimāsu vā //
1.80.d:
आभ्यामष्टादशक्लिपः स्याद्विंशत्यक्षरो मनुः ।
शालग्रामे मणौ यन्त्रे मण्डले प्रतिमासु वा ॥
1.80.m: With these two, the eighteen-syllabled mantra becomes a twenty-syllabled mantra. / In a Śālagrāma stone, in a jewel, in a yantra, in a sacred diagram, or in images,

1.80.s:
nityaṃ pūjā hareḥ kāryā na tu kevalabhūtale /
evaṃ yo bhajante kṛṣṇaṃ sa yāti paramāṃ gatim //
1.80.d:
नित्यं पूजा हरेः कार्या न तु केवलभूतले ।
एवं यो भजन्ते कृष्णं स याति परमां गतिम् ॥
1.80.m: the daily worship of Hari should be performed, but never on the bare ground. / He who worships Kṛṣṇa in this manner attains the supreme state.

1.80.s:
viṃśārṇasya munirbrahmā gāyatrī chanda īritam /
kṛṣṇaśca devatā kāmo bījaṃ śaktirdviṭho budhaiḥ //
1.80.d:
विंशार्णस्य मुनिर्ब्रह्मा गायत्री छन्द ईरितम् ।
कृष्णश्च देवता कामो बीजं शक्तिर्द्विठो बुधैः ॥
1.80.m: The sage of the twenty-syllabled mantra is declared to be Brahmā, the meter gāyatrī, / and Kṛṣṇa the deity; its seed is Kāma, and its power, according to the wise, is the two ṭhas [svāhā].

1.80.s:
rāmāgnivedavedābdhernetrārṇairaṅgakalpanam /
mūlena vyāpakaṃ kṛtvā manunā puṭitānatha //
1.80.d:
रामाग्निवेदवेदाब्धेर्नेत्रार्णैरङ्गकल्पनम् ।
मूलेन व्यापकं कृत्वा मनुना पुटितानथ ॥
1.80.m: The arrangement of the limbs is performed with groups of syllables numbering three, three, four, four, four, and two. / Having performed the comprehensive touch with the root mantra, one should then, enclosed by the mantra,

1.80.s:
mātṛkārṇānnyasettattatsthāneṣu susamāhitaḥ /
daśatattvāni vinyasya mūlena vyāpakaṃ caret //
1.80.d:
मातृकार्णान्न्यसेत्तत्तत्स्थानेषु सुसमाहितः ।
दशतत्त्वानि विन्यस्य मूलेन व्यापकं चरेत् ॥
1.80.m: place the syllables of the mātṛkā in their respective locations, fully concentrated. / Having placed the ten principles, one should perform the comprehensive touch with the root mantra.

1.80.s:
mantranyāsaṃ tataḥ kuryāddevatābhāvasiddhaye /
śīrṣe lalāṭe bhrūmadhye netrayoḥ karṇayostathā //
1.80.d:
मन्त्रन्यासं ततः कुर्याद्देवताभावसिद्धये ।
शीर्षे ललाटे भ्रूमध्ये नेत्रयोः कर्णयोस्तथा ॥
1.80.m: Then one should perform the mantra-placement for the attainment of identity with the deity: / on the head, forehead, between the eyebrows, on the two eyes, and on the two ears;

1.80.s:
nasorvakre ca cibuke kaṇṭhe dormūlake hṛdi /
udare nābhideśe ca liṅge mūlasaroruhe //
1.80.d:
नसोर्वक्रे च चिबुके कण्ठे दोर्मूलके हृदि ।
उदरे नाभिदेशे च लिङ्गे मूलसरोरुहे ॥
1.80.m: on the two nostrils, mouth, chin, throat, root of the arms, heart, / stomach, region of the navel, generative organ, and the lotus at the base;

1.80.s:
kaṭyāṃ jānvorjaṅghayośca gulphayoḥ pādayoḥ kramāt /
nyaseddhṛdantānmantrāṇāṃ sṛṣṭinyāso 'yamīritaḥ //
1.80.d:
कट्यां जान्वोर्जङ्घयोश्च गुल्फयोः पादयोः क्रमात् ।
न्यसेद्धृदन्तान्मन्त्राणां सृष्टिन्यासो ऽयमीरितः ॥
1.80.m: on the waist, knees, shanks, ankles, and feet in succession, / one should place the syllables of the mantra ending in ‘hṛt’ [namaḥ]; this is declared to be the placement of creation.

1.80.s:
hṛdaye codare nābhau liṅge mūlasaroruhe /
kaṭyāṃ jānvorjaṅghayośca gulphayoḥ pādayostathā //
1.80.d:
हृदये चोदरे नाभौ लिङ्गे मूलसरोरुहे ।
कट्यां जान्वोर्जङ्घयोश्च गुल्फयोः पादयोस्तथा ॥
1.80.m: On the heart, stomach, navel, generative organ, the lotus at the base, / on the waist, knees, shanks, ankles, and feet likewise;

1.80.s:
mūrdhni kapole bhrūmadhye netrayoḥ karṇayornasoḥ /
vadane cibuke kaṇṭhe dormūle vinyasetkramāt //
1.80.d:
मूर्ध्नि कपोले भ्रूमध्ये नेत्रयोः कर्णयोर्नसोः ।
वदने चिबुके कण्ठे दोर्मूले विन्यसेत्क्रमात् ॥
1.80.m: on the crown of the head, cheeks, between the eyebrows, on the eyes, ears, nostrils, / mouth, chin, throat, and root of the arms, one should place them in succession,

1.80.s:
namotānmantravarṇāṃśca sthitinyāso 'yamīritaḥ /
pādayorgulphayoścaiva jaṅghayorjānunostathā //
1.80.d:
नमोतान्मन्त्रवर्णांश्च स्थितिन्यासो ऽयमीरितः ।
पादयोर्गुल्फयोश्चैव जङ्घयोर्जानुनोस्तथा ॥
1.80.m: namely the syllables of the mantra ending in ‘namaḥ’; this is declared to be the placement of maintenance. / Then, on the feet, ankles, shanks, and knees;

1.80.s:
kaṭyāṃ mūle dhvaje nābhau jaṭhare hṛdaye punaḥ /
dormūle kaṇṭhadeśe ca cibuke vadane nasoḥ //
1.80.d:
कट्यां मूले ध्वजे नाभौ जठरे हृदये पुनः ।
दोर्मूले कण्ठदेशे च चिबुके वदने नसोः ॥
1.80.m: on the waist, base, penis, navel, belly, and again on the heart, / at the base of the arms, throat region, chin, mouth, nostrils,

1.80.s:
karṇayornetrayoścaiva bhrūmadhye niṭile tathā /
mūrdhni nyasenmantravarṇānsaṃhārākhyo 'yamīritaḥ //
1.80.d:
कर्णयोर्नेत्रयोश्चैव भ्रूमध्ये निटिले तथा ।
मूर्ध्नि न्यसेन्मन्त्रवर्णान्संहाराख्यो ऽयमीरितः ॥
1.80.m: ears, eyes, between the eyebrows, forehead, / and crown of the head, one should place the syllables of the mantra; this is declared to be the placement of withdrawal.

1.80.s:
punaḥ sṛṣṭisthitinyāsau vidhāya vaiṣṇavottamaḥ /
mūrtipañjaranāmānaṃ vinyasetpūrvavattataḥ //
1.80.d:
पुनः सृष्टिस्थितिन्यासौ विधाय वैष्णवोत्तमः ।
मूर्तिपञ्जरनामानं विन्यसेत्पूर्ववत्ततः ॥
1.80.m: Having again performed the placements of creation and maintenance, the best of Vaiṣṇavas / should then perform the placement called the cage of forms as before.

1.80.s:
punaḥ ṣaḍaṅgaṃ kṛtvātha dhyāyetkṛṣṇaṃ hṛdaṃbuje /
dvāravatyāṃ sahasrārkabhāsvarairbhavanottamaiḥ //
1.80.d:
पुनः षडङ्गं कृत्वाथ ध्यायेत्कृष्णं हृदंबुजे ।
द्वारवत्यां सहस्रार्कभास्वरैर्भवनोत्तमैः ॥
1.80.m: Having again performed the six limbs, one should meditate on Kṛṣṇa in the lotus of the heart: / in Dvāravatī, in a jewel pavilion surrounded by excellent palaces

1.80.s:
analpaiḥ kalpavṛkṣaiśca parīte maṇimaṇḍape /
jvaladratna mayastaṃbhadvāratoraṇakuḍyake //
1.80.d:
अनल्पैः कल्पवृक्षैश्च परीते मणिमण्डपे ।
ज्वलद्रत्न मयस्तंभद्वारतोरणकुड्यके ॥
1.80.m: radiant as a thousand suns and by many wish-granting trees, / with pillars, doorways, arched gateways, and walls made of flashing gems;

1.80.s:
phullapraphullasañcitravitānālaṃbimauktike /
padmarāgasthalīrājadratnasaṃghaiśca madhyataḥ //
1.80.d:
फुल्लप्रफुल्लसञ्चित्रवितानालंबिमौक्तिके ।
पद्मरागस्थलीराजद्रत्नसंघैश्च मध्यतः ॥
1.80.m: with pearls suspended from awnings decorated with blossoms in full bloom, / and in the middle, shining with heaps of gems on a floor of rubies;

1.80.s:
anāratagaladratnadhārāḍhyasvastastaroradhaḥ /
ratnapradīpāvalibhiḥ pradīpitadigantare //
1.80.d:
अनारतगलद्रत्नधाराढ्यस्वस्तस्तरोरधः ।
रत्नप्रदीपावलिभिः प्रदीपितदिगन्तरे ॥
1.80.m: beneath a heavenly tree rich with a stream of jewels continuously falling, / with the space of all directions illuminated by rows of jewel lamps;

1.80.s:
udyadādityasaṃkāśamaṇisiṃhāsanāṃbuje /
samāsīno 'cyuto dhyeyo drutahāṭakasannibhaḥ //
1.80.d:
उद्यदादित्यसंकाशमणिसिंहासनांबुजे ।
समासीनो ऽच्युतो ध्येयो द्रुतहाटकसन्निभः ॥
1.80.m: seated on the lotus of a jewel throne resembling the rising sun, / Acyuta is to be meditated upon, resembling molten gold,

1.80.s:
samānoditacandrārkataḍitkoṭisamadyutiḥ /
sarvāṅgasuṃdaraḥ saumyaḥ sarvābharaṇabhūṣitaḥ //
1.80.d:
समानोदितचन्द्रार्कतडित्कोटिसमद्युतिः ।
सर्वाङ्गसुंदरः सौम्यः सर्वाभरणभूषितः ॥
1.80.m: equal in brilliance to the simultaneously risen moon, sun, and ten million flashes of lightning, / handsome in every limb, gentle, adorned with all ornaments,

1.80.s:
pītavāsāḥ śaṅkhacakragadāṃbhojalasatkaraḥ /
anāhatocchaladratnadhāraughakalaśaṃ spṛśan //
1.80.d:
पीतवासाः शङ्खचक्रगदांभोजलसत्करः ।
अनाहतोच्छलद्रत्नधारौघकलशं स्पृशन् ॥
1.80.m: clad in yellow garments, his hands shining with the conch, discus, mace, and lotus, / touching the pitcher [flowing with] a continuous stream of overflowing jewels

1.80.s:
vāmapādāṃbujāgreṇa muṣṇatā pallavacchavim /
rukmiṇīsatyabhāme 'sya mūrdhni ratnaughadhārayā //
1.80.d:
वामपादांबुजाग्रेण मुष्णता पल्लवच्छविम् ।
रुक्मिणीसत्यभामे ऽस्य मूर्ध्नि रत्नौघधारया ॥
1.80.m: with the tip of his left lotus-foot that steals the splendor of a fresh sprout. / Rukmiṇī and Satyabhāmā, standing on his right and left,

1.80.s:
siṃcantyau dakṣavāmasthe svadosthakalaśotthayā /
nāgnajitī sunandā ca diśantyau kalaśau tayoḥ //
1.80.d:
सिंचन्त्यौ दक्षवामस्थे स्वदोस्थकलशोत्थया ।
नाग्नजिती सुनन्दा च दिशन्त्यौ कलशौ तयोः ॥
1.80.m: are showering upon his head a stream of jewels rising from pitchers held in their hands; / Nāgnajitī and Sunandā are offering pitchers to the two of them;

1.80.s:
tābhyāṃ ca dakṣavāmasthamitravindāsulakṣmaṇe /
ratnanadyāḥ samuddhṛtya ratnapūrṇauṃ ghaṭau tayoḥ //
1.80.d:
ताभ्यां च दक्षवामस्थमित्रविन्दासुलक्ष्मणे ।
रत्ननद्याः समुद्धृत्य रत्नपूर्णौं घटौ तयोः ॥
1.80.m: and to them, Mitravindā and Sulakṣmaṇā, standing on the right and left, / draw from the river of jewels two vessels full of jewels [and offer them];

1.80.s:
jāṃbavatī suśīlā ca diśantyau dakṣavāmake /
bahiḥ ṣoḍaśa sāhasrasaṃkhyākāḥ paritaḥ priyāḥ //
1.80.d:
जांबवती सुशीला च दिशन्त्यौ दक्षवामके ।
बहिः षोडश साहस्रसंख्याकाः परितः प्रियाः ॥
1.80.m: Jāmbavatī and Suśīlā on the right and left are offering [vessels to them]. / Outside, sixteen thousand beloved wives all around

1.80.s:
dhyeyāḥ kanakaratnaughadhārāyukkalaśojvalāḥ /
tadbahiścāṣṭanidhāyaḥ pūrayanto dhanairdharām //
1.80.d:
ध्येयाः कनकरत्नौघधारायुक्कलशोज्वलाः ।
तद्बहिश्चाष्टनिधायः पूरयन्तो धनैर्धराम् ॥
1.80.m: are to be meditated upon, shining with pitchers containing streams of heaps of gold and gems; / and outside of them, the eight treasures, filling the earth with riches;

1.80.s:
tadbahirvṛṣṇayaḥ sarve purovacca svarādayaḥ /
evaṃ dhyātvā japellakṣapañcakaṃ taddaśāṃśataḥ //
1.80.d:
तद्बहिर्वृष्णयः सर्वे पुरोवच्च स्वरादयः ।
एवं ध्यात्वा जपेल्लक्षपञ्चकं तद्दशांशतः ॥
1.80.m: outside of that, all the Vṛṣṇis, and the vowels and so forth as before. / Having thus meditated, one should recite the mantra five hundred thousand times, and one-tenth of that

1.80.s:
aruṇaiḥ kamalairhutvā pīṭhe pūrvodite yajet /
vilipya gandhapaṅkena likhedaṣṭadalāṃbujam //
1.80.d:
अरुणैः कमलैर्हुत्वा पीठे पूर्वोदिते यजेत् ।
विलिप्य गन्धपङ्केन लिखेदष्टदलांबुजम् ॥
1.80.m: one should offer into the fire with red lotuses, and worship on the seat described earlier. / Anointing it with fragrant paste, one should draw an eight-petaled lotus;

1.80.s:
karṇikāyāṃ ca ṣaṭkoṇaṃ sasādhyaṃ tatra manmatham /
śiṣṭaistu saptadaśabhirakṣarairveṣṭayetsvaram //
1.80.d:
कर्णिकायां च षट्कोणं ससाध्यं तत्र मन्मथम् ।
शिष्टैस्तु सप्तदशभिरक्षरैर्वेष्टयेत्स्वरम् ॥
1.80.m: and in the pericarp, a hexagon, and there Manmatha along with the objective; / and one should encircle the vowel with the remaining seventeen syllables.

1.80.s:
prāgrakṣo 'nilakoṇeṣu śriyaṃ śiṣṭeṣu saṃvidam /
ṣaṭsu saṃdhiṣu ṣaṭkarṇe kesareṣu triśastriśaḥ //
1.80.d:
प्राग्रक्षो ऽनिलकोणेषु श्रियं शिष्टेषु संविदम् ।
षट्सु संधिषु षट्कर्णे केसरेषु त्रिशस्त्रिशः ॥
1.80.m: In the east, south-west, and north-west corners [one should write] Śrī, and in the remaining [corners] Saṃvid; / at the six junctions, the six ears, and on the filaments three by three,

1.80.s:
vilikhetsmaragāyatrīṃ mālāmantraṃ dalāṣṭake /
ṣaṭūṣaḥ saṃlikhya tadbāhye veṣṭayenmātṛkākṣaraiḥ //
1.80.d:
विलिखेत्स्मरगायत्रीं मालामन्त्रं दलाष्टके ।
षटूषः संलिख्य तद्बाह्ये वेष्टयेन्मातृकाक्षरैः ॥
1.80.m: one should write the Smaragāyatrī; on the eight petals, the mālāmantra; / having written the six uṣma letters, outside of that one should surround it with the mātṛkā syllables.

1.80.s:
bhūbiṃbaṃ ca likhedbāhye śrīmāyādigvidikṣvapi /
bhūgrahaṃ caturasraṃ syādaṣṭavajravibhūṣitam //
1.80.d:
भूबिंबं च लिखेद्बाह्ये श्रीमायादिग्विदिक्ष्वपि ।
भूग्रहं चतुरस्रं स्यादष्टवज्रविभूषितम् ॥
1.80.m: And outside one should draw the earth-circle, and Śrī and Māyā in the cardinal and intermediate directions; / the earth enclosure should be four-cornered, adorned with eight vajras.

1.80.s:
etadyantraṃ hāṭakādipaṭṭeṣvālikhya pūrvavat /
saṃskṛtaṃ dhārayedyo vai sor'cyate tridaśairapi //
1.80.d:
एतद्यन्त्रं हाटकादिपट्टेष्वालिख्य पूर्ववत् ।
संस्कृतं धारयेद्यो वै सोर्ऽच्यते त्रिदशैरपि ॥
1.80.m: Having inscribed this yantra on a plate of gold or other metal, / whoever wears it consecrated as before is worshipped even by the thirty gods.

1.80.s:
syādgāyatrī vāmadevapuṣpabāṇau tu ṅeṃtimau /
vidmahedhīmahiyutau tanno 'naṅgaḥ pracodayāt //
1.80.d:
स्याद्गायत्री वामदेवपुष्पबाणौ तु ङेंतिमौ ।
विद्महेधीमहियुतौ तन्नो ऽनङ्गः प्रचोदयात् ॥
1.80.m: The gāyatrī is formed by ‘vāmadevāya’ and ‘puṣpabāṇāya’ in the dative case, / followed by ‘vidmahe’ and ‘dhīmahi’, and ‘tanno ’naṅgaḥ pracodayāt’.

1.80.s:
japyā japādau gopālamanūnāṃ janarañjanī /
hṛdayaṃ kāmadevāya ṅeṃtaṃ sarvajanapriyam //
1.80.d:
जप्या जपादौ गोपालमनूनां जनरञ्जनी ।
हृदयं कामदेवाय ङेंतं सर्वजनप्रियम् ॥
1.80.m: This mantra, pleasing to all people, should be recited at the beginning of recitation of the Gopāla mantras. / ‘Hṛdaya’ [om], to Kāmadeva in the dative case, ‘sarvajanapriya’ [beloved of all people],

1.80.s:
uktvā sarvajanānte tu saṃmohanapadaṃ tathā /
jvala jvala prajvaleti procya sarvajanasya ca //
1.80.d:
उक्त्वा सर्वजनान्ते तु संमोहनपदं तथा ।
ज्वल ज्वल प्रज्वलेति प्रोच्य सर्वजनस्य च ॥
1.80.m: and after ‘sarvajana’ having spoken the word ‘saṃmohana’, / and having uttered ‘jvala jvala prajvala’ [burn, burn, blaze up], and ‘sarvajanasya’,

1.80.s:
hṛdayaṃ mama ca brūyādvaśaṅkuruyugaṃ śiraḥ /
prokto madanamantro 'ṣṭacatvāriṃśadbhirakṣaraiḥ //
1.80.d:
हृदयं मम च ब्रूयाद्वशङ्कुरुयुगं शिरः ।
प्रोक्तो मदनमन्त्रो ऽष्टचत्वारिंशद्भिरक्षरैः ॥
1.80.m: one should say ‘hṛdayaṃ mama’, then the pair ‘vaśaṅkuru’ [make subject], and ‘śiras’ [svāhā]; / this Madanamantra of forty-eight syllables is proclaimed,

1.80.s:
japādau smarabījādyo jagattrayavaśīkaraḥ /
pīṭha prāgvatsamabhyarcya mūrti saṃkalpya mūlataḥ //
1.80.d:
जपादौ स्मरबीजाद्यो जगत्त्रयवशीकरः ।
पीठ प्राग्वत्समभ्यर्च्य मूर्ति संकल्प्य मूलतः ॥
1.80.m: having the seed of Smara at the beginning, bringing the three worlds under subjugation. / Having worshipped the ritual seat as before, and having projected the form from the root mantra,

1.80.s:
tatrāvāhyācyutaṃ bhaktyā sakalīkṛtya pūjayet /
āsanādivibhūṣāntaṃ punarnyāsakramādyajet //
1.80.d:
तत्रावाह्याच्युतं भक्त्या सकलीकृत्य पूजयेत् ।
आसनादिविभूषान्तं पुनर्न्यासक्रमाद्यजेत् ॥
1.80.m: having invoked Acyuta there with devotion, and having made him complete, one should worship him; / from the seat up to the ornaments, one should worship again in the order of placement:

1.80.s:
sṛṣṭiṃ sthitiṃ ṣaḍaṅgaṃ ca kirīṭaṃ kuṇḍaladvayam /
śaṅkhaṃ cakraṃ gadāṃ padmaṃ mālāṃ śrīvatsakaustubhau //
1.80.d:
सृष्टिं स्थितिं षडङ्गं च किरीटं कुण्डलद्वयम् ।
शङ्खं चक्रं गदां पद्मं मालां श्रीवत्सकौस्तुभौ ॥
1.80.m: creation, maintenance, the six limbs, crown, pair of earrings, / conch, discus, mace, lotus, garland, Śrīvatsa, and Kaustubha.

1.80.s:
gandhapuṣpaiḥ samabhyarcya mūlena vaiṣṇavottamaḥ /
ṣaṭkoṇeṣu ṣaḍaṅgāni digdaleṣu kramādyajet //
1.80.d:
गन्धपुष्पैः समभ्यर्च्य मूलेन वैष्णवोत्तमः ।
षट्कोणेषु षडङ्गानि दिग्दलेषु क्रमाद्यजेत् ॥
1.80.m: Having worshipped with perfumes and flowers using the root mantra, the best of Vaiṣṇavas / should worship the six limbs in the hexagons, and in the petals of the directions in sequence

1.80.s:
vāsudevādikānkoṇeṣu tu śāntyādikāṃstataḥ /
patrāgragā mahiṣyo 'ṣṭau yajetsādhakasattamaḥ //
1.80.d:
वासुदेवादिकान्कोणेषु तु शान्त्यादिकांस्ततः ।
पत्राग्रगा महिष्यो ऽष्टौ यजेत्साधकसत्तमः ॥
1.80.m: Vāsudeva and the others, and then Śānti and the others in the corners; / the best of practitioners should worship the eight chief queens situated at the tips of the petals.

1.80.s:
tataḥ ṣoḍaśasāhasraṃ sakṛdevārcayetpriyāḥ /
indranīlamukundāṃśca karālānandakacchapān //
1.80.d:
ततः षोडशसाहस्रं सकृदेवार्चयेत्प्रियाः ।
इन्द्रनीलमुकुन्दांश्च करालानन्दकच्छपान् ॥
1.80.m: Then he should worship the sixteen thousand beloved wives all at once; / and Indranīla, Mukunda, Karāla, Nanda, Kacchapa,

1.80.s:
śaṅkhapadmau tataḥ padmānnidhīnaṣṭau kramādyajet /
tadbahirlokapālāṃśca vajrādyānapi pūjayet //
1.80.d:
शङ्खपद्मौ ततः पद्मान्निधीनष्टौ क्रमाद्यजेत् ।
तद्बहिर्लोकपालांश्च वज्राद्यानपि पूजयेत् ॥
1.80.m: Śaṅkha, and Padma—then one should worship the eight lotus-treasures in sequence; / and outside of that, the guardians of the worlds, and also the vajra and other weapons.

1.80.s:
evaṃ saptāvṛttivṛtaṃ kṛṣṇamabhyarcya cādarāt /
prīṇayeddadhikhaṇḍājyamiśreṇa tu payoṃ'dhasā //
1.80.d:
एवं सप्तावृत्तिवृतं कृष्णमभ्यर्च्य चादरात् ।
प्रीणयेद्दधिखण्डाज्यमिश्रेण तु पयोंऽधसा ॥
1.80.m: Having thus reverently worshipped Kṛṣṇa surrounded by seven circuits, / one should gratify him with rice cooked in milk, mixed with curds, sugar candy, and ghee.

1.80.s:
divyopacāraṃ datvātha stutvā natvā ca keśavam /
udvāsayetsvahṛdaye parivāragaṇaiḥ saha //
1.80.d:
दिव्योपचारं दत्वाथ स्तुत्वा नत्वा च केशवम् ।
उद्वासयेत्स्वहृदये परिवारगणैः सह ॥
1.80.m: Then, having offered divine services of worship, and having praised and bowed down to Keśava, / one should dismiss him into one's own heart together with his attendants.

1.80.s:
nyasyātmānaṃ samabhyarcya tanmayo viharetsudhīḥ /
ratnābhiṣekadhyānejyā viṃśatyarṇāśrite ritā //
1.80.d:
न्यस्यात्मानं समभ्यर्च्य तन्मयो विहरेत्सुधीः ।
रत्नाभिषेकध्यानेज्या विंशत्यर्णाश्रिते रिता ॥
1.80.m: Having placed [the deity within], worshipping his own self, the wise man should conduct himself identified with Him. / This meditation and worship with the jewel-bath, based on the twenty-syllabled mantra, has been spoken.

1.80.s:
evaṃ yo bhajate mantraṃ sa samṛddheḥ padaṃ bhavet /
japahomārcanadhyānairyo manuṃ prajapedamum //
1.80.d:
एवं यो भजते मन्त्रं स समृद्धेः पदं भवेत् ।
जपहोमार्चनध्यानैर्यो मनुं प्रजपेदमुम् ॥
1.80.m: Whoever thus serves this mantra becomes an abode of prosperity. / Whoever recites this mantra with recitation, fire oblations, worship, and meditation,

1.80.s:
tadveśma pūryate ratnaiḥ ravarṇadhānyairanāratam /
pṛthvī pṛthvī kare tasya sarvasasyasamākulā //
1.80.d:
तद्वेश्म पूर्यते रत्नैः रवर्णधान्यैरनारतम् ।
पृथ्वी पृथ्वी करे तस्य सर्वसस्यसमाकुला ॥
1.80.m: his house is continuously filled with jewels, gold, and grains; / the broad earth, abundant with all crops, is in his hand.

1.80.s:
putrairmitraiḥ susaṃpannaḥ prayātyante parāṃ gatim /
vahnāvabhyarcya govindaṃ śuklapuṣpaiḥ satandulaiḥ //
1.80.d:
पुत्रैर्मित्रैः सुसंपन्नः प्रयात्यन्ते परां गतिम् ।
वह्नावभ्यर्च्य गोविन्दं शुक्लपुष्पैः सतन्दुलैः ॥
1.80.m: Abundantly endowed with sons and friends, he attains the supreme state in the end. / Having worshipped Govinda in the fire with white flowers and grains of rice,

1.80.s:
ājyāktairayutaṃ hutvā bhasma tanmūrdhni dhārayet /
tasyānnādisamṛddhiḥ syāttadūśe sarvayoṣitaḥ //
1.80.d:
आज्याक्तैरयुतं हुत्वा भस्म तन्मूर्ध्नि धारयेत् ।
तस्यान्नादिसमृद्धिः स्यात्तदूशे सर्वयोषितः ॥
1.80.m: and having offered ten thousand oblations mixed with clarified butter, he should place that ash on his head; / for him there will be an abundance of food and the like, and all women will come under his control.

1.80.s:
raktāṃbhojaistrimadhvaktairhunellakṣaṃ samāhitaḥ /
śriyā tasyaindramaiśvaryaṃ tṛṇaleśāyate dhruvam //
1.80.d:
रक्तांभोजैस्त्रिमध्वक्तैर्हुनेल्लक्षं समाहितः ।
श्रिया तस्यैन्द्रमैश्वर्यं तृणलेशायते ध्रुवम् ॥
1.80.m: Attentive, he should offer one hundred thousand oblations of red lotuses smeared with the three sweets; / before his splendor, Indra's royal sovereignty surely becomes as worthless as a blade of grass.

1.80.s:
trimadhvaktaiḥ sitaiḥ puṣpairaṣṭottarasahasrakam /
yo hunetpratyahaṃ māsātpurodhā nṛpaterbhavet //
1.80.d:
त्रिमध्वक्तैः सितैः पुष्पैरष्टोत्तरसहस्रकम् ।
यो हुनेत्प्रत्यहं मासात्पुरोधा नृपतेर्भवेत् ॥
1.80.m: Whoever should offer daily for a month one thousand and eight white flowers / smeared with the three sweets will become the royal priest of a king.

1.80.s:
evamādiprayogāṃśca sādhayenmanunāmunā /
mantrarājamatho vakṣye daśārṇaṃ sarvasiddhidam //
1.80.d:
एवमादिप्रयोगांश्च साधयेन्मनुनामुना ।
मन्त्रराजमथो वक्ष्ये दशार्णं सर्वसिद्धिदम् ॥
1.80.m: One should accomplish such rites through this mantra. / Now I will declare the king of mantras, consisting of ten syllables, which bestows all attainments.

1.80.s:
smṛtiḥ sadyānvitā sākṣirlohito janavallabhā /
pavano 'gnipriyānto 'yaṃ daśārṇo mantra īritaḥ //
1.80.d:
स्मृतिः सद्यान्विता साक्षिर्लोहितो जनवल्लभा ।
पवनो ऽग्निप्रियान्तो ऽयं दशार्णो मन्त्र ईरितः ॥
1.80.m: Smṛti accompanied by Sādya, Sākṣi, Lohita, Jana-vallabhā, / Pavana, and ending with the beloved of Agni—this is stated to be the ten-syllable mantra.

1.80.s:
nārado 'sya muniśchando virāṭ kṛṣṇo 'sya devatā /
kāmo bījaṃ vahnijāyā śaktiḥ proktā manīṣibhiḥ //
1.80.d:
नारदो ऽस्य मुनिश्छन्दो विराट् कृष्णो ऽस्य देवता ।
कामो बीजं वह्निजाया शक्तिः प्रोक्ता मनीषिभिः ॥
1.80.m: Its seer is Nārada; its metre is Virāj; its deity is Kṛṣṇa; / the seed-syllable is Kāma; the wife of Agni (Svāhā) is declared by the wise to be its śakti.

1.80.s:
ācakraṃ ca vicakraṃ ca sucakraṃ tadanantaram /
trailokyarakṣaṇaṃ cakramasurāntakagacakrakam //
1.80.d:
आचक्रं च विचक्रं च सुचक्रं तदनन्तरम् ।
त्रैलोक्यरक्षणं चक्रमसुरान्तकगचक्रकम् ॥
1.80.m: Ācakra, Vicakra, and thereafter Sucakra, / the Trailokyarakṣaṇa cakra, and the Asurāntakaga cakra—

1.80.s:
etairṅeṭhadvayāntaiśca cakraiḥ pañcāṅgakaṃ manoḥ /
tatastārapuṭaṃ mantraṃ vyāpayya karayostriśaḥ //
1.80.d:
एतैर्ङेठद्वयान्तैश्च चक्रैः पञ्चाङ्गकं मनोः ।
ततस्तारपुटं मन्त्रं व्यापय्य करयोस्त्रिशः ॥
1.80.m: with these names ending with the dative and two ṭha syllables (svāhā), the five limbs of the mantra are formed. / Then, having permeated both hands three times with the mantra enclosed by the praṇava,

1.80.s:
seṃdūnhṛdantānmantrārṇānpraṇavāntaritānnyaset /
dakṣāṅguṣṭhācca vāmāṅguṣṭhāntamaṅguliparvasu //
1.80.d:
सेंदून्हृदन्तान्मन्त्रार्णान्प्रणवान्तरितान्न्यसेत् ।
दक्षाङ्गुष्ठाच्च वामाङ्गुष्ठान्तमङ्गुलिपर्वसु ॥
1.80.m: he should ritually place on the joints of the fingers, from the right thumb to the left thumb, / the mantra's syllables accompanied by bindu, ending in hṛd (namaḥ), and separated by the praṇava.

1.80.s:
sṛṣṭinyāso 'yamuditaḥ sthitinyāso 'dhunocyate /
nyasedvāmakaniṣṭhādikaniṣṭāntaṃ sthitau sudhīḥ //
1.80.d:
सृष्टिन्यासो ऽयमुदितः स्थितिन्यासो ऽधुनोच्यते ।
न्यसेद्वामकनिष्ठादिकनिष्टान्तं स्थितौ सुधीः ॥
1.80.m: This is declared as the ritual placement of creation; now the ritual placement of preservation is told: / in preservation, the wise one should place from the left little finger to the [right] little finger.

1.80.s:
vāmāṅguṣṭhānnyaseddakṣāṃ guṣṭhāntaṃ saṃhṛtau tathā /
saṃhṛtirdeṣasaṃghātahāriṇī parikīrtitā //
1.80.d:
वामाङ्गुष्ठान्न्यसेद्दक्षां गुष्ठान्तं संहृतौ तथा ।
संहृतिर्देषसंघातहारिणी परिकीर्तिता ॥
1.80.m: And likewise, in dissolution, he should place from the left thumb to the right thumb; / the dissolution is proclaimed to remove multitudes of faults.

1.80.s:
vidyāpradaśca sṛṣṭyanto varṇināṃ śuddhacetasām /
sthityantaḥ syādgṛhasthānāmevaṃ kāmyādirūpataḥ //
1.80.d:
विद्याप्रदश्च सृष्ट्यन्तो वर्णिनां शुद्धचेतसाम् ।
स्थित्यन्तः स्याद्गृहस्थानामेवं काम्यादिरूपतः ॥
1.80.m: Ending with creation, it bestows knowledge upon pure-minded celibate students; / ending with preservation, it is for householders, in the form of desire-fulfillment and the like.

1.80.s:
saṃhārānte munīndrāṇāṃ viraktānāṃ ca sarvaśaḥ /
punaḥ sthitikrameṇārṇānmanoraṅguliṣu nyaset //
1.80.d:
संहारान्ते मुनीन्द्राणां विरक्तानां च सर्वशः ।
पुनः स्थितिक्रमेणार्णान्मनोरङ्गुलिषु न्यसेत् ॥
1.80.m: Ending with dissolution, it is for eminent sages and those completely detached. / He should again place the syllables of the mantra on the fingers in the order of preservation.

1.80.s:
punaścakraiśca pūrvoktaiḥ pañcāgaṃ karayornyaset /
tato mūlena puṭitānmātṛkārṇānsabindukān //
1.80.d:
पुनश्चक्रैश्च पूर्वोक्तैः पञ्चागं करयोर्न्यसेत् ।
ततो मूलेन पुटितान्मातृकार्णान्सबिन्दुकान् ॥
1.80.m: Again, with the previously stated cakras, he should place the five limbs on the hands. / Then the wise one, bowing low, should ritually place the mātṛkā syllables,

1.80.s:
vinyasenmātṛkānyāsasthāneṣu praṇataḥ sudhīḥ /
tatastārapuṭaṃ mūlaṃ vyāpakatvena vinyaset //
1.80.d:
विन्यसेन्मातृकान्यासस्थानेषु प्रणतः सुधीः ।
ततस्तारपुटं मूलं व्यापकत्वेन विन्यसेत् ॥
1.80.m: endowed with bindus and enclosed by the root mantra, upon the bodily sites of the mātṛkā ritual placement. / Then he should place the root mantra enclosed by the praṇava as an all-pervading placement.

1.80.s:
saṃhārasṛṣṭibhedena daśatattvāni vinyaset /
namontamūlamantrārṇapadāyāmyāni cātmane //
1.80.d:
संहारसृष्टिभेदेन दशतत्त्वानि विन्यसेत् ।
नमोन्तमूलमन्त्रार्णपदायाम्यानि चात्मने ॥
1.80.m: He should ritually place the ten principles according to the division into dissolution and creation, / extending the syllables and words of the root mantra ending in namaḥ for the self,

1.80.s:
matyantāni ca tattvāni pṛthivyādyāni ca kramāt /
pṛthvī jalaṃ tathā vahnirvāyurākāśameva ca //
1.80.d:
मत्यन्तानि च तत्त्वानि पृथिव्याद्यानि च क्रमात् ।
पृथ्वी जलं तथा वह्निर्वायुराकाशमेव च ॥
1.80.m: and the principles, beginning with earth, in order, ending in mati (buddhi): / earth, water, fire, wind, and ether,

1.80.s:
ahṝṅkāro mahattatvaṃ prakṛtiṃ puruṣaṃ param /
pravinyasenmastake ca netrayoḥ śrotrayornasoḥ //
1.80.d:
अहॄङ्कारो महत्तत्वं प्रकृतिं पुरुषं परम् ।
प्रविन्यसेन्मस्तके च नेत्रयोः श्रोत्रयोर्नसोः ॥
1.80.m: ego, the great principle, primordial nature, and the supreme Puruṣa; / he should place them on the head, eyes, ears, nostrils,

1.80.s:
vadane hṛdaye nābhau liṅge jānvośca pādayoḥ /
praṇavāntaritānvarṇānhṛdantānvijyasenmanoḥ //
1.80.d:
वदने हृदये नाभौ लिङ्गे जान्वोश्च पादयोः ।
प्रणवान्तरितान्वर्णान्हृदन्तान्विज्यसेन्मनोः ॥
1.80.m: mouth, heart, navel, genitals, knees, and feet, / placing the syllables of the mantra separated by the praṇava and ending in hṛd (namaḥ).

1.80.s:
sṛṣṭinyāso 'yamākhyātaḥ sthitinyāsaṃ śṛṇu dvija /
hṛdi nābhau dhvaje jānvoḥ pādayormastake punaḥ //
1.80.d:
सृष्टिन्यासो ऽयमाख्यातः स्थितिन्यासं शृणु द्विज ।
हृदि नाभौ ध्वजे जान्वोः पादयोर्मस्तके पुनः ॥
1.80.m: This has been declared as the ritual placement of creation; hear that of preservation, O twice-born: / on the heart, navel, penis, knees, feet, and then the head,

1.80.s:
netrayoḥ karṇayorghrāṇe vadane vinyasetkramāt /
padorjānvorliṅgadeśe nābhau hṛdi mukhe nasoḥ //
1.80.d:
नेत्रयोः कर्णयोर्घ्राणे वदने विन्यसेत्क्रमात् ।
पदोर्जान्वोर्लिङ्गदेशे नाभौ हृदि मुखे नसोः ॥
1.80.m: eyes, ears, nose, and mouth he should place them in order; / on the feet, knees, genital region, navel, heart, mouth, nostrils,

1.80.s:
karṇayornetrayormūrdhni saṃhārākhyo 'yamīritaḥ /
sṛṣṭyanto varṇināṃnyāsaḥ sthityantogṛhamedhinām //
1.80.d:
कर्णयोर्नेत्रयोर्मूर्ध्नि संहाराख्यो ऽयमीरितः ।
सृष्ट्यन्तो वर्णिनांन्यासः स्थित्यन्तोगृहमेधिनाम् ॥
1.80.m: ears, eyes, and top of the head—this is declared as that of dissolution. / Ritual placement ending in creation is for celibate students; ending in preservation, for householders;

1.80.s:
yatervairāgyayuktasya saṃhārāntaḥ prakīrtitaḥ /
caturddhā varṇināṃ caiva gṛhasthānāṃ ca pañcadhā //
1.80.d:
यतेर्वैराग्ययुक्तस्य संहारान्तः प्रकीर्तितः ।
चतुर्द्धा वर्णिनां चैव गृहस्थानां च पञ्चधा ॥
1.80.m: ending in dissolution, it is proclaimed for the renunciant endowed with detachment. / Ritual placement is stated in order to be auspicious fourfold for celibate students, fivefold for householders,

1.80.s:
yatīnāṃ ca tridhā nyāsaḥ prokto 'yaṃ kramataḥ śubhaḥ /
kecidvirakte gṛhage saṃhārāntaṃ vidurbudhāḥ //
1.80.d:
यतीनां च त्रिधा न्यासः प्रोक्तो ऽयं क्रमतः शुभः ।
केचिद्विरक्ते गृहगे संहारान्तं विदुर्बुधाः ॥
1.80.m: and threefold for renunciants. / Some wise men consider the one ending in dissolution to be for the detached householder.

1.80.s:
vibhūtipañjaraṃ nyāsaṃ kuryādiṣṭāptaye tataḥ /
manordaśāvṛttimayaṃ kṛṣṇasāṃnidhyakārakam //
1.80.d:
विभूतिपञ्जरं न्यासं कुर्यादिष्टाप्तये ततः ।
मनोर्दशावृत्तिमयं कृष्णसांनिध्यकारकम् ॥
1.80.m: Then, for attaining desired goals, one should perform the ritual placement called the Cage of Glory, / which consists of ten repetitions of the mantra and brings about the presence of Kṛṣṇa:

1.80.s:
ādhāre ca dhvaje nābhau hṛdi kaṇṭhe mukhe śaye /
ūrvośca kandharāyāṃ ca nābhau kukṣau tathā hṛdi //
1.80.d:
आधारे च ध्वजे नाभौ हृदि कण्ठे मुखे शये ।
ऊर्वोश्च कन्धरायां च नाभौ कुक्षौ तथा हृदि ॥
1.80.m: on the basal center, penis, navel, heart, throat, mouth, head, / thighs, neck, navel, abdomen, and likewise the heart,

1.80.s:
stanayoḥ pārśvayoḥ śroṇyormastakevadanetathā /
netrayoḥ karṇayornāsāpuṭayośca kapolayoḥ //
1.80.d:
स्तनयोः पार्श्वयोः श्रोण्योर्मस्तकेवदनेतथा ।
नेत्रयोः कर्णयोर्नासापुटयोश्च कपोलयोः ॥
1.80.m: breasts, flanks, hips, head, mouth, / eyes, ears, nostrils, and cheeks;

1.80.s:
evaṃ dakṣiṇadormūsasaṃdhyagreṣvaṅgulīṣu ca /
tataḥ śirasi tatpūrvādyāṃśāsu svakalāsu ca //
1.80.d:
एवं दक्षिणदोर्मूससंध्यग्रेष्वङ्गुलीषु च ।
ततः शिरसि तत्पूर्वाद्यांशासु स्वकलासु च ॥
1.80.m: likewise at the roots, joints, tips, and fingers of the right arm; / then on the head, in its parts beginning with the east, and on one's own faculties;

1.80.s:
doṣṇoḥ sakthnoḥ śirokṣyāsyakaṇṭhahṛjjaṭhareṣu ca /
mūlādhāre liṅgadeśe jānunoḥ pādayostathā //
1.80.d:
दोष्णोः सक्थ्नोः शिरोक्ष्यास्यकण्ठहृज्जठरेषु च ।
मूलाधारे लिङ्गदेशे जानुनोः पादयोस्तथा ॥
1.80.m: on the arms, thighs, head, eyes, mouth, throat, heart, and belly, / on the mūlādhāra, the genital region, knees, and feet,

1.80.s:
śrotragaṇḍāṃsavakṣojapārśvaliṅgeṣu vinyaset /
ūrvorjānvorjaṅghayośca pādayorvinyasetkramāt //
1.80.d:
श्रोत्रगण्डांसवक्षोजपार्श्वलिङ्गेषु विन्यसेत् ।
ऊर्वोर्जान्वोर्जङ्घयोश्च पादयोर्विन्यसेत्क्रमात् ॥
1.80.m: on the ears, cheeks, shoulders, chest, flanks, and penis; / on the thighs, knees, shanks, and feet he should place them in order.

1.80.s:
vibhūtipañjarākhyo 'yaṃ nyāsaḥ sarvārthasiddhidaḥ /
anena nyāsavaryeṇa sākṣātkṛṣṇatanurbhavet //
1.80.d:
विभूतिपञ्जराख्यो ऽयं न्यासः सर्वार्थसिद्धिदः ।
अनेन न्यासवर्येण साक्षात्कृष्णतनुर्भवेत् ॥
1.80.m: This ritual placement named the Cage of Glory bestows the fulfillment of all aims; / by this foremost of ritual placements, one becomes Kṛṣṇa's very form.

1.80.s:
mūrti pañjaranāmānaṃ nyāsaṃ pūrvoditaṃ nyaset /
tato daśāṅgapañcāṅgau nyāsavaryauṃ nyase kramāt //
1.80.d:
मूर्ति पञ्जरनामानं न्यासं पूर्वोदितं न्यसेत् ।
ततो दशाङ्गपञ्चाङ्गौ न्यासवर्यौं न्यसे क्रमात् ॥
1.80.m: He should perform the ritual placement named the Cage of the Form, which was spoken of earlier; / then he should perform in order the two foremost ritual placements of the ten limbs and the five limbs.

1.80.s:
hṛdi mūrdhni śikhāyāṃ ca sarvāṅge dikṣu pārśvayoḥ /
kaṭyāṃ pṛṣṭhe tathā mūrdhni vinyasedvaiṣṇavottamaḥ //
1.80.d:
हृदि मूर्ध्नि शिखायां च सर्वाङ्गे दिक्षु पार्श्वयोः ।
कट्यां पृष्ठे तथा मूर्ध्नि विन्यसेद्वैष्णवोत्तमः ॥
1.80.m: On the heart, head, crown-lock, the whole body, the directions, the flanks, / the waist, the back, and the head, the best of Vaiṣṇavas should place them.

1.80.s:
pañcāṅgāni nyasedbhūyaścakraiḥ prāgvatsamāhitaḥ /
anyo 'pyaṣṭādaśārṇoktaḥ kartavyo nyāsasaṃcayaḥ //
1.80.d:
पञ्चाङ्गानि न्यसेद्भूयश्चक्रैः प्राग्वत्समाहितः ।
अन्यो ऽप्यष्टादशार्णोक्तः कर्तव्यो न्याससंचयः ॥
1.80.m: Attentive, he should again place the five limbs with the cakras as before; / and the other collection of ritual placements taught for the eighteen-syllable mantra should also be performed.

1.80.s:
tataḥ kirīṭamantreṇa vyāpakaṃ racayetsudhīḥ /
veṇubilvādimudrāṃśca darśayetsādhakottamaḥ //
1.80.d:
ततः किरीटमन्त्रेण व्यापकं रचयेत्सुधीः ।
वेणुबिल्वादिमुद्रांश्च दर्शयेत्साधकोत्तमः ॥
1.80.m: Then the wise one should execute the all-pervading placement with the Kirīṭa mantra; / and the best of practitioners should display the mudrās such as the Flute and the Bilva.

1.80.s:
sudarśanasya mantreṇa kuryāddigbandhanaṃ tataḥ /
anaṅguṣṭhāśca ṛjavaḥ karaśākhā bhavanti cet //
1.80.d:
सुदर्शनस्य मन्त्रेण कुर्याद्दिग्बन्धनं ततः ।
अनङ्गुष्ठाश्च ऋजवः करशाखा भवन्ति चेत् ॥
1.80.m: Then he should perform the sealing of the directions with the mantra of Sudarśana. / If the fingers are straight without the thumbs,

1.80.s:
hṛnmudreyaṃ samākhyātā śiromudrā tathā bhavet /
adhoṅguṣṭhā tu yā muṣṭiḥ śikhāmudreyamīritā /
prasāritakarāṅgulyorvarmamudreyamīritā //
1.80.d:
हृन्मुद्रेयं समाख्याता शिरोमुद्रा तथा भवेत् ।
अधोङ्गुष्ठा तु या मुष्टिः शिखामुद्रेयमीरिता ।
प्रसारितकराङ्गुल्योर्वर्ममुद्रेयमीरिता ॥
1.80.m: this is declared as the mudrā of the heart, and the mudrā of the head is likewise; / the fist with the thumb pointed downward is declared as the mudrā of the crown-lock; / the extended fingers of the hands are declared as the mudrā of the armor.

1.80.s:
nārācamuṣṭyā dhṛtabāhuyugmaḥ aṅguṣṭhatarjanyudito dhvanistu /
viṣvagvimuktā kathitāstramudrā yatrākṣiṇī tarjanimadhyame ca //
1.80.d:
नाराचमुष्ट्या धृतबाहुयुग्मः अङ्गुष्ठतर्जन्युदितो ध्वनिस्तु ।
विष्वग्विमुक्ता कथितास्त्रमुद्रा यत्राक्षिणी तर्जनिमध्यमे च ॥
1.80.m: Both arms held in the Nārāca fist, with a snap produced by thumb and forefinger / released all around—this is described as the mudrā of the weapon, where the forefinger and middle finger are the eyes.

1.80.s:
oṣṭhe vāmakarāṅguṣṭo lagnastasya kaniṣṭikā /
dakṣiṇāṅguṣṭasaṃsaktā tatkaniṣṭhā prasāritā //
1.80.d:
ओष्ठे वामकराङ्गुष्टो लग्नस्तस्य कनिष्टिका ।
दक्षिणाङ्गुष्टसंसक्ता तत्कनिष्ठा प्रसारिता ॥
1.80.m: The thumb of the left hand touching the lip, its little finger / joined to the right thumb, with that [right] little finger extended,

1.80.s:
tarjanī madhyamānāmā kiñcitsakuñcya cālitā /
veṇumudreyamuditā suguptā preyasī hareḥ /
nocyante tatra siddhatvānmālāśrīvatsakaustubhāḥ //
1.80.d:
तर्जनी मध्यमानामा किञ्चित्सकुञ्च्य चालिता ।
वेणुमुद्रेयमुदिता सुगुप्ता प्रेयसी हरेः ।
नोच्यन्ते तत्र सिद्धत्वान्मालाश्रीवत्सकौस्तुभाः ॥
1.80.m: and the forefinger, middle finger, and ring finger slightly bent and moved— / this is declared as the Flute mudrā, very secret and beloved of Hari; / the Garland, the Śrīvatsa, and the Kaustubha are not described here, as they are already established.

1.80.s:
vāmāṅguṣṭhaṃ samudraṃ tamaparakarāṅguṣṭhakenātha baddhvā saṃpīḍyāgraṃ ca dakṣāṅgulibhirapi ca tāṃ vāmahastāṅgulībhiḥ /
gāḍhaṃ baddhvā svakīye hṛdayasarasije sthāpayetkāmabījaṃ proccāryaiṣā tu gopyā sakalasukhakarī vilvamudrā munīndraiḥ //
1.80.d:
वामाङ्गुष्ठं समुद्रं तमपरकराङ्गुष्ठकेनाथ बद्ध्वा संपीड्याग्रं च दक्षाङ्गुलिभिरपि च तां वामहस्ताङ्गुलीभिः ।
गाढं बद्ध्वा स्वकीये हृदयसरसिजे स्थापयेत्कामबीजं प्रोच्चार्यैषा तु गोप्या सकलसुखकरी विल्वमुद्रा मुनीन्द्रैः ॥
1.80.m: Having enclosed that left thumb with the thumb of the other hand, pressing the tip with the right fingers and with the fingers of the left hand, / and having clasped it tightly, one should place it upon one's own heart-lotus, uttering the Kāma seed-syllable; this Bilva mudrā, bestower of all happiness, is to be kept secret by eminent sages.

1.80.s:
kāyena manasā vācā yatpāpaṃ samupārjitam /
mudrāyā jñāna mātreṇa sarvaṃ nāśamupaiṣyati //
1.80.d:
कायेन मनसा वाचा यत्पापं समुपार्जितम् ।
मुद्राया ज्ञान मात्रेण सर्वं नाशमुपैष्यति ॥
1.80.m: Whatever sin has been acquired through body, mind, or speech / will entirely perish by the mere knowledge of this mudrā.

1.80.s:
dhyānaṃ japastrikālārcā kāryā pūrvoditā manoḥ /
sarveṣvekaḥ kramaḥ prokto daśārṇāṣṭādaśārṇayoḥ //
1.80.d:
ध्यानं जपस्त्रिकालार्चा कार्या पूर्वोदिता मनोः ।
सर्वेष्वेकः क्रमः प्रोक्तो दशार्णाष्टादशार्णयोः ॥
1.80.m: The meditation, recitation, and worship at the three junctures of the day should be performed as previously declared for the mantra; / for all [procedures], a single order of ritual is taught for both the ten-syllable and the eighteen-syllable mantras.

1.80.s:
evaṃ siddhe manau mantrī prayogānkartumarhati /
uddaṇḍabāhudordaṃhadhṛtagovarddhanācalam //
1.80.d:
एवं सिद्धे मनौ मन्त्री प्रयोगान्कर्तुमर्हति ।
उद्दण्डबाहुदोर्दंहधृतगोवर्द्धनाचलम् ॥
1.80.m: When the mantra has thus been perfected, the practitioner is fit to perform magical applications: / [Meditating on him] whose arm is raised high to uphold Mount Govardhana with the force of his hand,

1.80.s:
anyahastāgulīvyaktasvaravaṃśārpitānanam /
dhyāyankṛṣṇaṃ japenmantraṃ vrajecchatraṃ vinā sudhīḥ //
1.80.d:
अन्यहस्तागुलीव्यक्तस्वरवंशार्पिताननम् ।
ध्यायन्कृष्णं जपेन्मन्त्रं व्रजेच्छत्रं विना सुधीः ॥
1.80.m: Whose face is applied to the flute whose notes are sounded by the fingers of his other hand— / Meditating on Kṛṣṇa, the wise man should recite the mantra and go forth even without an umbrella;

1.80.s:
varṣavātāśanibhyo 'pi bhayaṃ tasya na jāyate /
moghamedhaughavrātādgagatendraṃ taṃ smaranhunet //
1.80.d:
वर्षवाताशनिभ्यो ऽपि भयं तस्य न जायते ।
मोघमेधौघव्राताद्गगतेन्द्रं तं स्मरन्हुनेत् ॥
1.80.m: No danger from rain, wind, or lightning arises for him. / Remembering him as Indra in the sky [scattering] dense masses of deceptive clouds, one should offer oblation:

1.80.s:
loṇairayutasaṃkhyaiḥ syādanāvṛṣṭirna saṃśayaḥ /
krīḍantamarkajātīre majjanasnāpanādibhiḥ //
1.80.d:
लोणैरयुतसंख्यैः स्यादनावृष्टिर्न संशयः ।
क्रीडन्तमर्कजातीरे मज्जनस्नापनादिभिः ॥
1.80.m: With lumps of salt ten thousand in number, a drought will surely occur. / [Meditating on him] sporting on the bank of the Yamunā by plunging, bathing, and the like,

1.80.s:
tacchīkarajalāsāraiḥ sicyamānaṃ priyājanaiḥ /
dhyātvāyutaṃ payaḥ siktairhunedvā nīratarpaṇaiḥ //
1.80.d:
तच्छीकरजलासारैः सिच्यमानं प्रियाजनैः ।
ध्यात्वायुतं पयः सिक्तैर्हुनेद्वा नीरतर्पणैः ॥
1.80.m: Being sprinkled by his beloved women with showers of spray and water— / Having meditated on him, one should offer ten thousand oblations sprinkled with milk, or with libations of water:

1.80.s:
vṛṣṭirbhavatyakāle 'pi mahatī nātra saṃśayaḥ /
sadāhamohairārtasya visphoṭakajvarādibhiḥ //
1.80.d:
वृष्टिर्भवत्यकाले ऽपि महती नात्र संशयः ।
सदाहमोहैरार्तस्य विस्फोटकज्वरादिभिः ॥
1.80.m: Even out of season, a great rain will occur; there is no doubt about this. / For one afflicted with burning and delirium, with smallpox, fever, and the like,

1.80.s:
amumeva smaranmūrdhni japecchāntirbhavetkṣaṇāt /
athavā garuḍārūḍhaṃ pradyumnabalasaṃyutam //
1.80.d:
अमुमेव स्मरन्मूर्ध्नि जपेच्छान्तिर्भवेत्क्षणात् ।
अथवा गरुडारूढं प्रद्युम्नबलसंयुतम् ॥
1.80.m: Remembering this very [form], one should recite [the mantra] over his head; relief will come in an instant. / Or meditating on Acyuta mounted upon Garuḍa, accompanied by Pradyumna and Balarāma,

1.80.s:
nijajvaraniṣpiṣṭajvarābhiṣṭutamacyutam /
dhyātvā mūrdhni japenmantraṃ jvaramukto bhavejjvarī //
1.80.d:
निजज्वरनिष्पिष्टज्वराभिष्टुतमच्युतम् ।
ध्यात्वा मूर्ध्नि जपेन्मन्त्रं ज्वरमुक्तो भवेज्ज्वरी ॥
1.80.m: Praised by the fever that was crushed by his own fever, / One should recite the mantra over the head [of the patient]; the fevered one will be freed from fever.

1.80.s:
dhyātvaivamagnāvabhyarcya yathoktaiścaturaṅgulaiḥ /
juhuyādamṛtākhaṇḍairayutaṃ jvaraśāntaye //
1.80.d:
ध्यात्वैवमग्नावभ्यर्च्य यथोक्तैश्चतुरङ्गुलैः ।
जुहुयादमृताखण्डैरयुतं ज्वरशान्तये ॥
1.80.m: Having meditated in this way and worshipped him in the fire, / One should offer ten thousand oblations of pieces of guḍūcī measuring four finger-breadths as prescribed, for the pacification of fever.

1.80.s:
śilīmukhavinirbhinnabhīṣmatāpaharaṃ harim /
dhyātvā japetspṛśannārtaṃ pāṇibhyāṃ jvaraśāntaye //
1.80.d:
शिलीमुखविनिर्भिन्नभीष्मतापहरं हरिम् ।
ध्यात्वा जपेत्स्पृशन्नार्तं पाणिभ्यां ज्वरशान्तये ॥
1.80.m: Meditating on Hari who removed the distress of Bhīṣma pierced by arrows, / One should recite [the mantra] while touching the afflicted person with both hands, for the pacification of fever.

1.80.s:
sāṃdīpanāya dadataṃ putraṃ dhyātvāyutaṃ hunet /
yathoktairamṛtākhaṇḍairapamṛtyunivṛttaye //
1.80.d:
सांदीपनाय ददतं पुत्रं ध्यात्वायुतं हुनेत् ।
यथोक्तैरमृताखण्डैरपमृत्युनिवृत्तये ॥
1.80.m: Meditating on him giving back his son to Sāṃdīpani, one should offer ten thousand oblations / With pieces of guḍūcī as prescribed, for the averting of untimely death.

1.80.s:
sapārthaṃ mṛtaputrāyārpayantaṃ ca dvijanmane /
sutaṃ dhyātvā japellakṣaṃ putrapautrādivṛddhaye //
1.80.d:
सपार्थं मृतपुत्रायार्पयन्तं च द्विजन्मने ।
सुतं ध्यात्वा जपेल्लक्षं पुत्रपौत्रादिवृद्धये ॥
1.80.m: Meditating on him together with Arjuna restoring the dead sons to the twice-born man, / One should recite one hundred thousand times, for the increase of sons, grandsons, and progeny.

1.80.s:
putrajīvaphalairhutvāyutaṃ madhurasaṃplutaiḥ /
tatkāṣṭhairedhite vahnau sutāndīrghāyuṣo labhet //
1.80.d:
पुत्रजीवफलैर्हुत्वायुतं मधुरसंप्लुतैः ।
तत्काष्ठैरेधिते वह्नौ सुतान्दीर्घायुषो लभेत् ॥
1.80.m: Having offered ten thousand oblations of putrajīva fruits drenched in honey, / Into a fire kindled with its wood, one will obtain long-lived sons.

1.80.s:
kṣīradruktvāthasaṃpūrṇamabhyarcya kalaśaṃ niśi /
prātarjjaptvāyutaṃ nārīmabhiṣiñceddiṣaḍdinam //
1.80.d:
क्षीरद्रुक्त्वाथसंपूर्णमभ्यर्च्य कलशं निशि ।
प्रातर्ज्जप्त्वायुतं नारीमभिषिञ्चेद्दिषड्दिनम् ॥
1.80.m: Having worshipped a water-pot filled with the decoction of milky trees at night, / And reciting ten thousand times in the morning, one should sprinkle a woman for twelve days.

1.80.s:
evaṃ kṛte tu vandhyāpi labhetputrāṃścirāyuṣaḥ /
prātarvācaṃyamāśvatthadalasaṃpuṭakaṃ jalam //
1.80.d:
एवं कृते तु वन्ध्यापि लभेत्पुत्रांश्चिरायुषः ।
प्रातर्वाचंयमाश्वत्थदलसंपुटकं जलम् ॥
1.80.m: When this is done, even a barren woman will obtain long-lived sons. / In the morning, keeping silence, a woman desiring a son should drink water

1.80.s:
aṣṭottaraśataṃ japtaṃ māsaṃ putrārthinī pibet /
sarvalakṣaṇasaṃpannaṃ vandhyāpi labhate sutam //
1.80.d:
अष्टोत्तरशतं जप्तं मासं पुत्रार्थिनी पिबेत् ।
सर्वलक्षणसंपन्नं वन्ध्यापि लभते सुतम् ॥
1.80.m: Over which the mantra has been recited one hundred and eight times, from a cup formed of an aśvattha leaf, for a month; / Even a barren woman obtains a son endowed with all auspicious marks.

1.80.s:
jitvā kṛtyāṃ kāśirājapreṣitāṃ ca nijāriṇaḥ /
tejasā tasya nagaraṃ dahṝntaṃ bhāvayanharim //
1.80.d:
जित्वा कृत्यां काशिराजप्रेषितां च निजारिणः ।
तेजसा तस्य नगरं दहॄन्तं भावयन्हरिम् ॥
1.80.m: Contemplating Hari, who conquered the kṛtyā-spell sent by the king of Kāśī against his enemies, / And burned down his city with his splendor,

1.80.s:
hunetsaptadinaṃ mantrī susnehāktaiśca sarṣapaiḥ /
kṛtyākartāramevāsmai kupitā nāśayeddhruvam //
1.80.d:
हुनेत्सप्तदिनं मन्त्री सुस्नेहाक्तैश्च सर्षपैः ।
कृत्याकर्तारमेवास्मै कुपिता नाशयेद्ध्रुवम् ॥
1.80.m: The practitioner should offer oblations for seven days with mustard seeds well-smeared with oil; / Becoming enraged, she will surely destroy the very instigator of the hostile spell.

1.80.s:
badarīdrumasaṃkīrṇe sthitaṃ divyāśrame śubhe /
spṛśantaṃ karapadmābhyāṃ ghaṇṭākarṇakalevaram //
1.80.d:
बदरीद्रुमसंकीर्णे स्थितं दिव्याश्रमे शुभे ।
स्पृशन्तं करपद्माभ्यां घण्टाकर्णकलेवरम् ॥
1.80.m: [Meditating on him] seated in an auspicious, divine hermitage crowded with badarī trees, / Touching the body of Ghaṇṭākarṇa with his lotus-hands,

1.80.s:
dhyātvaivaṃ juhuyāllakṣaṃ tilaistrimadhurāplutaiḥ /
mahāpāpayuto 'pyevaṃ pūto bhavati tatkṣaṇāt //
1.80.d:
ध्यात्वैवं जुहुयाल्लक्षं तिलैस्त्रिमधुराप्लुतैः ।
महापापयुतो ऽप्येवं पूतो भवति तत्क्षणात् ॥
1.80.m: Having meditated thus, one should offer one hundred thousand oblations with sesame seeds drenched in the three sweets; / Even if burdened with great sins, one is purified in that very moment.

1.80.s:
dyūtāsaktau rukmibalau dveṣayantaṃ hariṃ smaran /
juhuyādiṣṭayordviṣṭyai gulikā gomayodbhavāḥ //
1.80.d:
द्यूतासक्तौ रुक्मिबलौ द्वेषयन्तं हरिं स्मरन् ।
जुहुयादिष्टयोर्द्विष्ट्यै गुलिका गोमयोद्भवाः ॥
1.80.m: Remembering Hari who caused mutual hatred between Rukmin and Balarāma when they were intent on gambling, / One should offer pellets made of cow dung to create enmity between two intended persons.

1.80.s:
nityaṃ sahasraṃ saptāhānmitho vidveṣayedarīn /
varṣantaṃ garuḍārūḍhaṃ jvaladagnimukhaiḥ śaraiḥ //
1.80.d:
नित्यं सहस्रं सप्ताहान्मिथो विद्वेषयेदरीन् ।
वर्षन्तं गरुडारूढं ज्वलदग्निमुखैः शरैः ॥
1.80.m: Offering a thousand every day for seven days, one turns enemies against each other. / [Meditating on him] mounted on Garuḍa, showering arrows with blazing tips of fire,

1.80.s:
dhāvantaṃ ripusaṃghātamanudhāvatamacyutam /
dhyātvā saptasahasraṃ tu japenmantramananyadhīḥ //
1.80.d:
धावन्तं रिपुसंघातमनुधावतमच्युतम् ।
ध्यात्वा सप्तसहस्रं तु जपेन्मन्त्रमनन्यधीः ॥
1.80.m: Pursuing the host of enemies as they flee—having meditated on Acyuta thus, / One should recite the mantra seven thousand times with single-minded focus;

1.80.s:
uccāṭanaṃ bhavatyeva śatrūṇāṃ saptabhirdinaiḥ /
dhyāyannutkṣiptavatsaṃ tu kapitthaphalahāriṇam //
1.80.d:
उच्चाटनं भवत्येव शत्रूणां सप्तभिर्दिनैः ।
ध्यायन्नुत्क्षिप्तवत्सं तु कपित्थफलहारिणम् ॥
1.80.m: The eradication and driving away of enemies surely takes place within seven days. / Meditating on him throwing the calf and knocking down the kapittha fruits,

1.80.s:
prajapedayutaṃ śatrumuñcāṭayati tatkṣaṇāt /
ātmānaṃ kaṃsamathanaṃ dhyāyanmañcānnipātitam //
1.80.d:
प्रजपेदयुतं शत्रुमुञ्चाटयति तत्क्षणात् ।
आत्मानं कंसमथनं ध्यायन्मञ्चान्निपातितम् ॥
1.80.m: One should recite ten thousand times; he drives away the enemy in an instant. / Meditating on oneself as the slayer of Kaṃsa, and on Kaṃsa thrown down from his dais,

1.80.s:
kaṃsātmānaṃ vyakarṣantaṃ gatāsuṃ taṃ japenmanum /
ripujanmarkṣavṛkṣotthasamidbhirayutaṃ niśi //
1.80.d:
कंसात्मानं व्यकर्षन्तं गतासुं तं जपेन्मनुम् ।
रिपुजन्मर्क्षवृक्षोत्थसमिद्भिरयुतं निशि ॥
1.80.m: And dragging him as his life has departed, one should recite the mantra; / At night, with fuel sticks taken from the tree corresponding to the enemy's birth-star,

1.80.s:
juhuyādevamugro 'pi sapatno nidhanaṃ vrajet /
athavā niṃbatailāktairhunedhobhirakṣajaiḥ //
1.80.d:
जुहुयादेवमुग्रो ऽपि सपत्नो निधनं व्रजेत् ।
अथवा निंबतैलाक्तैर्हुनेधोभिरक्षजैः ॥
1.80.m: One should offer ten thousand oblations; thus even a fierce rival will go to destruction. / Alternatively, one should offer oblations with terminalia fuel-sticks smeared with neem oil;

1.80.s:
ayutaṃ niyato rātrau mārayedacirādarīn /
niśādiṣṭadalavyoṣakārpāsāsthikarairniśi //
1.80.d:
अयुतं नियतो रात्रौ मारयेदचिरादरीन् ।
निशादिष्टदलव्योषकार्पासास्थिकरैर्निशि ॥
1.80.m: Being self-controlled, one should offer ten thousand oblations at night; he destroys enemies before long. / At night, with cotton seeds, three pungents, and crushed [enemy-marked] leaves,

1.80.s:
hunederaṇḍatailāktaiḥ śmaśāne ripuśāntaye /
na śastaṃ māraṇaṃ karma kuryyāñcedayutaṃ hunet //
1.80.d:
हुनेदेरण्डतैलाक्तैः श्मशाने रिपुशान्तये ।
न शस्तं मारणं कर्म कुर्य्याञ्चेदयुतं हुनेत् ॥
1.80.m: Smeared with castor oil, one should offer oblations in a cremation ground for the pacification of enemies. / Destructive sorcery is not recommended; but if one performs it, one should offer ten thousand oblations,

1.80.s:
pāyasairvā hunettāvacchāntaye śāntamānasaḥ /
pārijātaharaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ dhyāyan lakṣaṃ japenmanum //
1.80.d:
पायसैर्वा हुनेत्तावच्छान्तये शान्तमानसः ।
पारिजातहरं कृष्णं ध्यायन् लक्षं जपेन्मनुम् ॥
1.80.m: Or, with a pacified mind, offer the same number of oblations of milk-rice for pacification. / Meditating on Kṛṣṇa seizing the pārijāta tree, one should recite the mantra one hundred thousand times;

1.80.s:
sarvatraiva jayastasya na kadāpi parājayaḥ /
vyākhyāmudrākaraṃ kṛṣṇaṃ rathasthaṃ bhāvayañjapet //
1.80.d:
सर्वत्रैव जयस्तस्य न कदापि पराजयः ।
व्याख्यामुद्राकरं कृष्णं रथस्थं भावयञ्जपेत् ॥
1.80.m: His victory is assured everywhere; never does defeat occur. / Meditating on Kṛṣṇa standing in the chariot, his hand forming the exposition gesture,

1.80.s:
pārthe diśantaṃ gītārthaṃ dharmavṛddhyai sumānavaḥ /
pāvāśapuṣpairmadhvaktairlakṣaṃ vidyāptayehunet //
1.80.d:
पार्थे दिशन्तं गीतार्थं धर्मवृद्ध्यै सुमानवः ।
पावाशपुष्पैर्मध्वक्तैर्लक्षं विद्याप्तयेहुनेत् ॥
1.80.m: Instructing Arjuna in the meaning of the Gītā for the increase of righteousness, a good man should recite [it]; / To attain knowledge, he should offer one hundred thousand oblations with palāśa flowers smeared with honey.

1.80.s:
rāṣṭrapūrgrāmavastūnāṃ śarīrasyāpi rakṣaṇe /
viśvarūpadhara prodyadbhānukoṭisamaprabham //
1.80.d:
राष्ट्रपूर्ग्रामवस्तूनां शरीरस्यापि रक्षणे ।
विश्वरूपधर प्रोद्यद्भानुकोटिसमप्रभम् ॥
1.80.m: For the protection of a realm, a city, a village, of possessions, and also of one's own body: / Meditating on the one who bears the cosmic form, radiant as ten million rising suns,

1.80.s:
agrīṣomātmakaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ drutacāmīkaraprabham /
arkāgnidyotitāsyāṅghriṃpraṅkaja divyabhūṣaṇam //
1.80.d:
अग्रीषोमात्मकं कृष्णं द्रुतचामीकरप्रभम् ।
अर्काग्निद्योतितास्याङ्घ्रिंप्रङ्कज दिव्यभूषणम् ॥
1.80.m: Whose nature is the sun and the moon, Kṛṣṇa, lustrous as molten gold, / Whose lotus face and feet are illuminated by sun and fire, adorned with divine ornaments,

1.80.s:
nānāyudhadharaṃ prāptaṃ viśvākāśāvakāśakam /
dhyātvā lakṣa japenmantraṃ rakṣaṇāya samāhitaḥ //
1.80.d:
नानायुधधरं प्राप्तं विश्वाकाशावकाशकम् ।
ध्यात्वा लक्ष जपेन्मन्त्रं रक्षणाय समाहितः ॥
1.80.m: Bearing various weapons, pervading the space of the entire universe— / Having meditated on him, one should recite the mantra one hundred thousand times with concentrated mind for protection.

1.80.s:
raktairvanyaprasūnairyo dinādau pūjayeddharim /
dinamadhyoktavidhinā japedaṣṭottaraṃ śatam //
1.80.d:
रक्तैर्वन्यप्रसूनैर्यो दिनादौ पूजयेद्धरिम् ।
दिनमध्योक्तविधिना जपेदष्टोत्तरं शतम् ॥
1.80.m: He who worships Hari at daybreak with red forest flowers, / And recites one hundred and eight times according to the rule prescribed for midday,

1.80.s:
sahasramaṇḍalānmantrī vaśayenmukharāndvijān /
jātipuṣpaiḥ kṣatriyāṃśca gopaveṣadharaṃ smaran //
1.80.d:
सहस्रमण्डलान्मन्त्री वशयेन्मुखरान्द्विजान् ।
जातिपुष्पैः क्षत्रियांश्च गोपवेषधरं स्मरन् ॥
1.80.m: Will, within a period of one thousand days, subjugate eloquent brāhmaṇas. / [Subjugating] kṣatriyas with royal jasmine flowers, remembering him in the attire of a cowherd;

1.80.s:
dhyāyan krīḍārataṃ kṛṣṇaṃ raktairaśvāripuṣpakaiḥ /
vaśayedvaiśyajātīyān śūdrānnīlotpalaiḥ smaran //
1.80.d:
ध्यायन् क्रीडारतं कृष्णं रक्तैरश्वारिपुष्पकैः ।
वशयेद्वैश्यजातीयान् शूद्रान्नीलोत्पलैः स्मरन् ॥
1.80.m: Meditating on Kṛṣṇa engaged in sports, with red oleander flowers / One can subjugate the vaiśya class; and śūdras, remembering him, with blue lotuses;

1.80.s:
gītanṛtyarataṃ śvetapuṣpaiḥ sājyaiśca tandulaiḥ /
hutvānvahaṃ saptadinaṃ bhasma bhāle ca mūrddhani //
1.80.d:
गीतनृत्यरतं श्वेतपुष्पैः साज्यैश्च तन्दुलैः ।
हुत्वान्वहं सप्तदिनं भस्म भाले च मूर्द्धनि ॥
1.80.m: [Meditating on him] delighting in song and dance, with white flowers and grains of rice mixed with ghee, / Having offered oblations daily for seven days, placing the ashes on one's forehead and on the crown of the head,

1.80.s:
dhārayanvaśayetkāntāṃ sāpi tadvatpatiṃ dhruvam /
tāṃbūlaṃ kusumaṃ vāsoṃ'janaṃ candanameva ca //
1.80.d:
धारयन्वशयेत्कान्तां सापि तद्वत्पतिं ध्रुवम् ।
तांबूलं कुसुमं वासोंऽजनं चन्दनमेव च ॥
1.80.m: One will surely subjugate his beloved woman, and she likewise her husband. / Betel, a flower, a garment, collyrium, and sandalwood paste—

1.80.s:
sahasraṃ manunā japtaṃ dadyādyasmai narāya ca /
so 'cirādeṣa vaśagaḥ saputrapaśubāndhavaḥ //
1.80.d:
सहस्रं मनुना जप्तं दद्याद्यस्मै नराय च ।
सो ऽचिरादेष वशगः सपुत्रपशुबान्धवः ॥
1.80.m: Whatever person one gives these to, over which the mantra has been recited a thousand times, / That person quickly comes under one's control, along with sons, cattle, and kinsmen.

1.80.s:
vṛndāraṇyasthitaṃ dhyāyanballavīsaṃyutaṃ harim /
apāmārgasamidbhistu hutvā tu vaśayejjagat //
1.80.d:
वृन्दारण्यस्थितं ध्यायन्बल्लवीसंयुतं हरिम् ।
अपामार्गसमिद्भिस्तु हुत्वा तु वशयेज्जगत् ॥
1.80.m: Meditating on Hari dwelling in the Vṛndā forest accompanied by the cowherd women, / And offering oblations with apāmārga fuel-sticks, one subjugates the world.

1.80.s:
saṃprāpya sadguror dīkṣāṃ kṛṣṇaṃ yo vidhināmunā /
arcayedvaiṣṇavaśreṣṭhaḥ so 'ṣṭasiddhīśvaro bhavet //
1.80.d:
संप्राप्य सद्गुरोर् दीक्षां कृष्णं यो विधिनामुना ।
अर्चयेद्वैष्णवश्रेष्ठः सो ऽष्टसिद्धीश्वरो भवेत् ॥
1.80.m: Having obtained initiation from a true teacher, the best of Vaiṣṇavas who worships Kṛṣṇa / According to this method becomes the master of the eight supernatural powers.

1.80.s:
tasya darśanamātreṇa vādino niṣprabhāḥ smṛtāḥ /
vasetsarasvatī vakre gṛhe cāpi sabhāsadaḥ //
1.80.d:
तस्य दर्शनमात्रेण वादिनो निष्प्रभाः स्मृताः ।
वसेत्सरस्वती वक्रे गृहे चापि सभासदः ॥
1.80.m: By merely looking at him, disputants are said to lose their luster; / Sarasvatī dwells in his mouth, and assembly members in his home.

1.80.s:
bhuktvā nānāvidhānbhogānante viṣṇupadaṃ vrajet //
iti śrībṛhannāradīyapurāṇe pūrvabhāge tṛtīyapāde kṛṣṇamantranirūpaṇaṃ nāmāśītitamo 'dhyāyaḥ
1.80.d:
भुक्त्वा नानाविधान्भोगानन्ते विष्णुपदं व्रजेत् ॥
इति श्रीबृहन्नारदीयपुराणे पूर्वभागे तृतीयपादे कृष्णमन्त्रनिरूपणं नामाशीतितमो ऽध्यायः
1.80.m:
Having enjoyed various pleasures, he attains the abode of Viṣṇu at the end.

Thus ends the eightieth chapter, titled "Exposition of the Mantras of Kṛṣṇa," in the third quarter of the first section in the venerable Bṛhannāradīya Purāṇa.
